A Upcoming Azzedine Alaïa Retrospective Goes Beyond the Bandage Dress

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1466 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the bandage dress.
  • According to recent reports, alaïa’s designs “were completely shocking” to the public at the time, recounts Laura Camerlengo, curator in charge of costume and textile arts at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco.
  • Recent findings suggest that born in 1935 in Tunis, Alaïa first trained as a sculptor, a background evident in his body of work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the bandage dress. The zipper dress. The perforated leather. The jersey hoods. The peplummed chemises. Azzedine Alaïa’s designs may not look so radical now, but almost 50 years ago, he changed the collective tide of fashion. The bandage dress is perhaps the most pervasive bit of his legacy, and it is emblematic of how the late French-Tunisian designer ushered in a new body-conscious silhouette in the ’80s, one made possible by technological innovations in materials that sculpted without any rigid, waist-cinching structure.

According to recent reports, alaïa’s designs “were completely shocking” to the public at the time, recounts Laura Camerlengo, curator in charge of costume and textile arts at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco. She has spent the past four years developing a new exhibition titled “Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion,” the first major U.S. retrospective dedicated to the work of the famed couturier. It opened November 21.

Recent findings suggest that born in 1935 in Tunis, Alaïa first trained as a sculptor, a background evident in his body of work. In 1956, he decamped to Paris to pursue fashion full-time. After a brief internship at the house of Christian Dior, he worked under Guy Laroche for less than two years before taking on his own private clients, then launching his own atelier in the late ’70s. From there, he built the house we know today. His obsession with construction and material innovation allowed him to both celebrate and liberate the female form. He passed away in late 2017 at the age of 82.

In a recent development, camerlengo first encountered Alaïa’s work as an assistant on the “Patrick Kelly Runway of Love” exhibition that the Philadelphia Museum of Art organized in 2014. “I was intrigued by how many of the new designers in Paris at this time were being supported by US consumers and retailers,” she indicates. After ascending to her new position in San Francisco years later, she cold-emailed Olivier Saillard, director of the Azzedine Alaïa Foundation in Paris. He was intrigued, and the two began working together on the exhibition almost immediately.

According to recent reports, the exhibition focuses on 80 garments from across Alaïa’s celebrated career, divided over a series of archetypes—the bandage dresses, sculptures and shapes, black and white, silhouettes and suiting, and construction and craftsmanship—to explore how his design aesthetic evolved. Interspersed are designs worn by devotees like Tina Turner, Grace Jones, and Rihanna. One final gallery highlights his personal collections of the work of designers he most admired, like Christian Dior and Charles James.

Ahead, Camerlengo speaks to Bazaar about curating the fresh exhibition, contextualizing Alaïa’s work in today’s fashion landscape, and his enduring legacy.

The exhibition is not chronological. We look at a series of Alaïa’s archetypes like the bandage dress to explore how his design aesthetic evolved over the course of his career. He often himself said that he didn’t want to conform to seasonal trends; he was more interested in the evolution of his designs. And so the gallery demonstrates a mix of objects dating from the 1980s to his final collection in 2017, and they’re largely grouped by type.

In a recent development, when you come in, you are greeted by Grace Jones, as we say, and the seminal purple hooded bandage dress from the fashion Oscars [a French event held in 1985]. As you move through, you’ll see a selection of the zipper dresses, the chiffon gowns, and other works that tie into some of the other themes. In each space, we mix the time periods. And that was something Alaïa himself often remarked. [He had a running joke that he didn’t know his own age.] He often said he was “as old as the pharaohs.” Basically, time was a construct for him.

That’s a great word for it. We could think of the popularity of the Japanese fashion designers who obscured women’s bodies with their voluminous styles. We could think of the suiting of the period. The 1970s is this period of workplace equality. Women are wearing suits in the style of masculine dress, but that also means they're obscuring their bodies. And then we can think of pop culture. I always think of Diane Keaton’s Annie Hall in 1977.

Some of the individuals I interviewed for my catalog text who were retailers in San Francisco at the time described Alaïa's designs as being like a whiplash. It was a complete 180 from the styles that they had gotten used to over the past decade, which also includes the rise of T-shirts and jeans for women as a mode of dress.

So here you have these very sexy, very form-fitting clothes. And part of the Alaïa aesthetic, as I see it, is the reclamation of the gaze. Rather than women being passively looked at—usually by men—they are instead commanding their own agency. As you mentioned, it was completely earth-shattering and very shocking at the time.

Azzedine Alaïa was one of the few couturiers who could work completely by the methods of tailoring and by draping, start to finish, from the initial concept to the final product. I did not fully appreciate his tailoring and the suits he constructed beforehand. We have a selection of them in a gallery of the exhibition, and their construction is absolutely incredible. The way they fit the body, the way they uplift and empower women through cloth—again, very antithetical to what we saw in the decades prior in the 1970s. These are very form-fitting, tailored at the waist, but they have soft feminine touches as well that give you this interesting mix of femininity and strength at the same time.

Very notable. We talk in the first gallery about how women, speaking generally, were the architects of his life. He learned to sew from his sister, who was working for a seamstress. He was encouraged by a local midwife in Tunisia to go to school at the Institute of Fine Arts. She helped him forge his papers to read 16—he was only 15 at the time. He learned his skills, not in formal training, but from women in Tunisia.

And then his early work was supported by a lot of leading figures of international society, including various Rothschilds, the French performer Arletty, the Swedish American actress Greta Garbo, and that's all before he even started to work formally under his own label in the 1980s. Of course, in the 1980s, he adopts Naomi Campbell, who becomes his protégé. He has close relationships with Grace Jones and Tina Turner. They were hugely vital to him. In the exhibition, the clear invisible mounts that we use are actually based on the body of Naomi Campbell.

Probably the Grace Jones bandage dress from the fashion Oscars in 1985. Not only is it the progression of the bandage dress style that he experiments with throughout the course of the 1980s, but it represents a key moment in his career where he receives two very high accolades as part of the fashion Oscars and he’s recognized for his genius.

As far as the designs themselves, I think we would consider the bandage dress, for example, an iconic symbol of late 20th- and 21st-century fashion developed by Azzedine Alaïa, but of course iterated upon extensively. We've seen surges and resurgences in its popularity ever since.

It has been revealed that and then as far as the landscape of the broader fashion system, Alaïa was someone who really eschewed seasonal calendars and trends. He was unconcerned with making things for the market. He often wanted to just produce clothes and share them when he felt they were ready. So I think his method of working foreshadows some of the conversations we’re having now about the overproduction of fashion and the overconsumption of fashion, even the detrimental environmental impacts that we see connected to it. He was really a forerunner, in a sense, to question the fashion system.

You can see how he really studied the construction of other garments and then adapted it in his own way in his designs. For example, he admired the work of Charles James, the great American fashion designer who was able to manipulate fabric to achieve weightless volume. And you see in Alaïa's own collections as he continues in his career, he does radial tucks and pleating to also get a certain amount of weightless volume in some of his gowns, very much in the spirit of James.

In a recent development, I hope our visitors appreciate the artistry of his work, first and foremost, and also the importance of handcraftsmanship. We are increasingly in an age of technology, especially with the rise of AI. What he created by his own hand is something that we can really marvel at.

According to recent reports, owen Wilson is a spiritual guy—and long has been. That’s why it fits so naturally that he would star in a golf series for Apple TV, Stick, in which his character, Pryce Cahill, is often searching to find his perfect zen. And as Wilson jokes, he’s started calling himself “Johnny Flowstate” on the green as he talks to himself through shots.

“I just believe there’s something more going on that you can tap into,” he tells Esquire editor in chief Michael Sebastian on the latest episode of “What I’ve Learned.” The fifty-five-year-old actor, best known for his roles in The Royal Tenenbaums, Wedding Crashers, and Midnight in Paris, even admits that he found himself reaching into the beyond for advice from his late father, TV executive Robert Wilson, in a moment of pure panic before hosting Saturday Night Live in 2021.

“He was already gone at that point, but the night before I was freaking out like, I don’t know if I can do this. I was so nervous, and I was thinking a lot about my dad,” Wilson notes. The two were incredibly close, and he reveals that his father actually worked with him and his brothers, actors Luke Wilson and Andrew Wilson, on several of their films. One of which was Wes Anderson’s Rushmore, in which their father wrote Bill Murray’s now-iconic church address to the students: “Take dead aim on the rich boys.".

So, as Wilson found himself full of doubt and fear the night before hosting SNL, he recalls looking up and “literally asking [his father] for help” before falling asleep. “I woke up, just incredibly calm, and I had this conviction of this joke my dad would say that needed to go in my monologue.”.

What was the joke? “That he was the charter member of the 3970 club,” Wilson indicates, “which stood for ‘three sons, nine high schools, seven colleges, and zero degrees.’”.

In a recent development, “That wasn’t something he was proud of,” Wilson continues. “That was his way to cope with disappointment, but you could almost say that that joke was worth us having all those struggles in school because that joke has lived longer than another diploma would have.” You can watch the episode above as well as listen on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

Sources indicate that luckily, it all worked out for the Wilson brothers. Next up, Owen is set to appear in season 2 of Stick on Apple TV and the Meet the Parents legacy sequel, Focker-in-Law with Ben Stiller. He also takes a liking to Esquire’s suggestion of a Christmas movie with another one of his longtime collaborators, Wes Anderson, in the episode.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s one of the biggest relationships of my life,” Wilson says of his friendship with the director. “Had I gotten into one of the colleges that I applied to, I would never have met Wes. And there’s something I always say to my boys—the idea that you can’t do it alone. If there’s something going wrong, I know I can always call and he’ll always be there for me.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.
  • In a recent development, the venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025.
  • A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

In a recent development, the venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025. The share of enterprises paying for AI rose from 55% to 65%.

A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.

Sources indicate that menlo's methodology describes revenue figures as annualized run rates. The $176.8 billion estimate therefore should not be read as $176.8 billion already spent during the first nine months of 2026.

The report also distinguishes unusually heavy spenders from the typical respondent. Average reported spending reached 4.7 times the prior year's level, while the median reached 2.2 times. That gap suggests a smaller group of large spenders drove the average substantially.

Sources indicate that the practical implication is that an industry growth figure may be a poor benchmark for an individual organization's budget. Buyers need to understand their own workload growth and the results it produces.

"Agents are changing the economics of software," Menlo principal Derek Xiao said in the firm's announcement.

Menlo reports that agents account for 80% of tokens on OpenRouter, a service providing access to multiple models. That measures activity on one platform, rather than all enterprise AI use. Token consumption also measures processing volume, rather than completed business outcomes.

Industry observers note that an agent that makes repeated attempts can consume more resources without delivering proportionately more value. For procurement teams, the relevant comparison is consequently the cost of completing acceptable work, including the review it requires.

According to recent reports, menlo estimates that Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google capture 69% of enterprise AI deployment spending. That measure is distinct from their shares of enterprise language-model API spending, a narrower category. The figures should not be used interchangeably.

The report draws on a Morning Consult survey of nearly 400 U.S. enterprise decision-makers responsible for more than $4 billion in AI spending. Market totals are modeled estimates informed by surveys, public filings, and third-party reports. Menlo discloses investments in Anthropic and OpenRouter.

A separate announcement from Information Services Group describes buyers putting more emphasis on the economics and reliability of production deployments. ISG claims ongoing security and observability work remains necessary as organizations scale.

In a recent development, that provides a useful distinction between market demand and business value. Suppliers can generate growing revenue while customers still determine which deployments justify the cost.

For enterprise leaders, the upcoming spending estimate strengthens the case for examining usage beyond license counts. It leaves the harder purchasing question with the customer: How much worthwhile work did the increased spending actually buy?

Menlo's State of Enterprise AI report is available here.

7 Home Organizing Trends That Will Be EVERYWHERE in 2027, According to Pros

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although trends prevail in the interior design world, they also can find their way into other areas beyond decor—such as home organization.
  • As we look to the year ahead, four professional organizers are here to share what they think will be the top organizing trends.
  • While AI has been all over the place, from work to our personal lives—it appears to be tapering off, according to Lenora O’Keith, decluttering and organizing expert and owner of Aronel Home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although trends prevail in the interior design world, they also can find their way into other areas beyond decor—such as home organization. Creating orderly spaces can make life a lot easier. While tried-and-true solutions are still around, there are always fresh ways to tackle organizing projects.

As we look to the year ahead, four professional organizers are here to share what they think will be the top organizing trends.

While AI has been all over the place, from work to our personal lives—it appears to be tapering off, according to Lenora O’Keith, decluttering and organizing expert and owner of Aronel Home.

In a recent development, “AI and smart home solutions were everywhere at the beginning of the year, but there’s definitely been a lot of AI fatigue and a push for ‘dumb tech’ lately,” she shares. “When working with clients, a lot of them are over AI being added into everything. They just want simple solutions that work.” This can include things like setting up a household command center and labeling storage containers.

Industry observers note that moving has traditionally been a stressful experience that you were expected to figure out on your own—but that may be changing. Allison Flinn, owner of Reclaim Professional Organizing, claims that more people are taking advantage of organizing services when they move.

“You can pack and unpack, but you won't truly have a fully functional and an organized latest home if you haven't decluttered prior to moving or aren't intentional during the unpacking process by implementing a system that truly works for your lifestyle,” she says.

Instead of doing what a lot of us do—devising storage systems for each individual space—2027 may welcome the idea that you should treat your home as an entire unit to be organized.

Recent findings suggest that michelle Urban, owner and founder of The Organized House, claims that people are increasingly not treating each room as its own one-off organizing project. She says that instead, they’re looking at how belongings move from one space to another and where they need to be throughout the day. For instance, items like backpacks, shoes, and sports gear may land in the entry, get stored in the garage, and need to be back by the door the next morning.

“When those spaces are planned together, the system supports the family’s routine instead of just moving things from one pile to another,” Urban indicates.

Viewed more holistically, experts are also seeing that organizing isn’t just an occasional task, but something to stay on top of each week. “I think more homeowners will begin to view organization as ongoing home maintenance rather than a one-time project,” claims Ashley Bailey, founder and professional organizer at Everything Orderly. “Just like other aspects of maintaining a home, organizing requires occasional attention as our lives and needs change.”.

It has been revealed that flinn says that more and more people are outsourcing household tasks to a home manager or home concierge. In addition to handling things like doing laundry, returning packages, and making doctor’s appointments, these professionals can also help you organize your home in just a few hours a week.

Eco-friendly everything is still as popular as ever, and it even applies to how we organize our homes. While O’Keith says that sustainability never really goes out of style, homeowners are increasingly turning to eco-friendly organizing products—specifically, by avoiding plastic and embracing natural materials like bamboo, rattan, and sea grass for baskets and bins.

But she claims that there is a exception for basements and attics. “I always recommend heavy-duty plastic storage [for these areas],” O’Keith says. “Since those spaces deal with dampness, temperature changes, and pests, other materials could get damaged easily.”.

While it can be lovely to live in a well-designed, beautiful home, if there isn’t function, you might make your daily life more difficult. That’s why people are going beyond Instagram-ready interiors and are wrapping in plenty of function.

Urban believes that progressively more people are bringing functional storage into a room’s design, and it isn’t just an add-on.

According to recent reports, “A credenza can hold games in the living room; a dining room buffet can store wrapping paper and party decor between celebrations,” Urban points out. “As rooms take on more jobs, people want storage that looks like it belongs and does a useful job.”.

As we head into 2027, people are thinking about their budgets more and more, which is why using items you already have as storage solutions is cost-effective.

“I'm seeing more clients interested in making better use of what they already own rather than automatically purchasing new organizing products,” Bailey states. For instance, she recently took on a project that transformed a playroom, but used items the family already had.

Recent findings suggest that “Sometimes the best solution isn't another organizing product. It's rethinking how you're using the space and what you already have,” she claims. “I think we'll see more emphasis on thoughtful editing and repurposing before purchasing something new.”.

If you’re a fan of The Hunting Wives, chances are you’re probably invested in the on-screen affair between Brittany Snow and Malin Akerman’s characters, Sophie and Margo. But off screen, both actresses are happily in relationships—Akerman with her husband of eight years, Jack Donnelly, and Snow with latest fiancé Hunter Moreno.

Sources indicate that snow confirmed the engagement news on a November 19 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, when Barrymore asked her directly, “Are you recently engaged?” The Hunting Wives star replied, “You know what? For the first time, I’m gonna tell you, I’m gonna tell you. Yes, we’re engaged, yeah. I haven’t said it before. It’s okay. It’s not that big of a secret. I mean, like, who cares?”.

Industry observers note that in talking about her husband-to-be, Snow revealed that the two began dating during the filming of the first season of The Hunting Wives. “He’s the best,” she grinned, adding that Akerman was one of the people to encourage the relationship early on.

According to recent reports, akerman, who was also a guest on the show, added, “We all met him. We got to be, like, the first ones to judge him. Like, ‘This is the right energy for you.’”.

The costars then playfully admitted they jokingly refer to the cast’s boyfriends and husbands as “The Hunting Husbands.”.

Industry observers note that so, who is Snow’s fiancé, Hunter Moreno? Ahead, everything to know about the creative and their relationship.

It has been revealed that based in Los Angeles, Moreno began his career directing and filming YouTube videos for influencers before expanding into music, directing videos for artists including Dasha, Charlie Puth, Ava Max, and Machine Gun Kelly. Along with his video credentials, he’s also photographed artists from Selena Gomez to Lizzo, Renee Rapp, and Cara Delevingne. Moreno has also shot fashion editorials and campaigns for publications and brands including Vogue and Madewell.

In 2018, Moreno founded Make Sure Your Friends Are Okay (MSYFAO), a mental health awareness organization that sells clothing and merch, with a portion of its proceeds benefiting various mental health charities.

The initiative is rooted in Moreno’s own experiences with mental health. In an Instagram post shared in May, he opened up about his struggles with depression and the personal reason he started the organization. “In 2018 I started Make Sure Your Friends Are Okay for a selfish reason I didn’t say out loud: I hoped someone would check on me while I was struggling with my own mental health complications and depression,” he wrote. He went on to encourage others to check in on the people they care about and make conversations about mental health more normalized.

Mental health advocacy is also crucial to Snow, who co-founded September Letters in 2020. The letter-writing platform, which has partnered with the Mental Health Coalition, aims to help end the stigma surrounding mental health.

Moreno and Snow were first publicly linked in October 2024, when they were photographed kissing while walking through New York City. During a 2026 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show, Snow confirmed that the two began dating during the filming of The Hunting Wives’ first season, which began in 2024.

Sources indicate that on March 28, 2026, Snow made their relationship Instagram official—though it was slyly packed into a massive carousel post. Amongst the photos from her birthday celebration in the desert were two photos of Snow and Moreno, a mirror selfie and a photo of the two posing with her dog.

Though Moreno’s Instagram is mostly dedicated to his professional work, in September, he uploaded a carousel of photos taken of Snow while traveling from Italy to France.

In a recent development, rumors of an engagement first sparked between Snow and Moreno in November 2025, when a video shared by DeuxMoi showed Claire Danes chatting with Snow on a red carpet and seemingly congratulating her on her engagement. “You’re engaged?!” Danes exclaimed during the exchange. Nearly a year later, Snow finally confirmed the news during an appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show.

“You know what? For the first time, I’m gonna tell you, I’m gonna tell you. Yes, we’re engaged, yeah,” Snow stated when Barrymore asked her directly. “I haven’t said it before. It’s okay. It’s not that substantial of a secret. I mean, like, who cares?”.

While gushing about her fiancé alongside Barrymore and her Hunting Wives costar Akerman, Snow called Moreno “the best.” She also revealed that Akerman played a role in their love story, encouraging Snow to pursue the relationship early on.

Which Glossier Perfume Is the Best? I Sniffed and Ranked All 5 in Honor of Their Black Friday Sale

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
  • In a recent development, before Glossier You had its sisters (Doux, Rêve, Fleur, and Soie), it was the most popular perfume in the world.
  • All this fame led to its 2024 iterations, Glossier You Doux and Glossier You Rêve, both of which received rave reviews online and in the Cosmo office when I waltzed around spraying it to get everyone's take.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

In a recent development, before Glossier You had its sisters (Doux, Rêve, Fleur, and Soie), it was the most popular perfume in the world. Truly, I couldn’t walk down my college campus without the familiar scent wafting up my nose. More than the inside of a Forever 21 and Svedka Strawberry Lemonade, it became a signature scent of the late 2010s and early 2020s; like the Abercrombie and Hollister of the early aughts. You rewrote what perfume could be: subdued and skin-like, with a smooth freshness that just smells like you, but better. Since then, it’s been named one of the best perfumes by Cosmo editors and a 2025 Readers’ Choice Award.

All this fame led to its 2024 iterations, Glossier You Doux and Glossier You Rêve, both of which received rave reviews online and in the Cosmo office when I waltzed around spraying it to get everyone's take. In 2025, the brand expanded with Glossier You Fleur, a salty and floral iteration of the original. Now, Glossier has debuted its 2026 flanker: Glossier You Soie, a beachy white floral. But how do they all compare? Which scent remains on top? Reviews, right this way. But first: FYI, Glossier is running its Black Friday sale right now, offering 25% off everything, including fragrance. If you ever wanted to try Glossier You or any of its flankers, now’s the time.

Recent findings suggest that all Glossier You perfumes have the same essential DNA. With ambroxan and ambrette notes that smell musky, sweaty, sweet, and warm, they're meant to be an upgraded, more effervescent version of your skin. But that's where the similarities end with all of the version of You, as they really do have their own distinct scent family and vibe. Keep scrolling for our full reviews (and ranking) of each scent:.

Key notes: Salt, cashmeran, apricot, ylang-ylang, osmanthus, ambroxan.

I was fully prepared to hate this scent, considering I'm not a floral lover. But Fleur isn't your typical floral perfume. Sure, there's osmanthus, but it's heavy on the apricot and salt, giving the scent a way more beachy vibe than garden-y one IMO. I saw someone compare it to the vibes of Call Me By Your Name: juicy fruits, blooming flowers, ocean air, all whipping through your hair as you bike along the Italian countryside with a lover. I see the vision. It's the sweet smell of yearning, baby.

It has been revealed that I wore this perfume on a press trip with a handful of beauty editors from other publications, and everyone kept stopping to ask me what fragrance I was wearing. "Wow?! Glossier?!" They couldn't believe their noses. Not because other Glossier perfumes aren't good, but because this is so unique that they thought it'd be from some $$$ niche fragrance house. Of every Glossier perfume, this stands out amongst the rest. The only con is that it might not be the best in the depths of fall and winter unless I want a little escapism. But for spring and summer, this will have a dedicated space on my vanity.

Key notes: Palo santo, sweet violet, frankincense, myrrh, ambroxan, ambrette.

Recent findings suggest that glossier You Doux feels like the rich aunt of the family, but in a "quiet luxury," reserved kinda vibe. Like wrapping yourself in a $2,000 cream sweater that feels like butter against your skin. Or the inside of an ultra-chic hotel lounge you need a membership card to enter. It's for the people who loved the original You in high school or college and want to level up their signature scent to match their big adult salary (without, ya know, paying a fortune, ofc—these perfumes are all under $80 for a 1.7 oz).

It has been revealed that cosmo editors were addicted to this perfume since it's so subdued (naturally, "doux" means soft in French). Truly, I didn't find a single team member who didn't like it. Editor-in-Chief Willa Bennett immediately spritzed this on her skin (bold) and loved how light it was. I picked up on the palo santo right away, which reminds me a lot of Le Labo Santal 33 (which makes sense, considering Frank Voelkl, the perfumer of Santal 33, is also the nose behind these two fragrances). Assistant news editor Sam Olson agreed, noting that it smells like if you layered O.G. Glossier You with Santal 33—"just without all the gaslighting and trauma of the ex everyone has who wears the Le Labo scent," she says. Real!

It has been revealed that shopping editor Hannah Oh messaged me the night after the test to praise the longevity too. "I just smelled my wrist, and HOURS LATER, it smells so yummy," she wrote. Best part about this fragrance to me is how versatile it is. I could wear this for every single occasion, any time of year, with any outfit, and always feel like it's right.

Key notes: Rice milk, tiare water, ambroxan, evening jasmine.

Recent findings suggest that of course, a Glossier beachy scent fits the whole “clean girl” thing. This isn’t tropical or sunscreen-y. Don’t expect a perfume akin to a piña colada. Instead, Soie (which means “silk” in French) is a solar-inspired white floral perfume with notes of rice, milk, and water. There’s a creamy, savory undertone that makes this smell clean, but not sharp. It’s like flowers soaked in milk. Baby-soft and a little warm, but with a burst of energy from an opening bergamot note. To me, this smells like plopping your butt in the sand and watching the waves crash. There’s minimal sweetness, rather relying on the lactonic notes to create a creamy throughline.

Sounds like it should be at the top of the list, right? Well, it just doesn’t last that long on my skin. It would be fantastic for someone who prefers a super subtle perfume. But I just wish it didn’t disappear after a few hours and need to be reapplied. The performance just isn’t up to par with Doux and Fleur, but its scent makes up for this compared to the other two from the line.

Key notes: Iris, pink pepper, ambroxan, ambrette.

According to recent reports, hey, it's an O.G. for a reason. Glossier You completely changed the fragrance game when it debuted in 2017. You know those pH-balanced blushes and lipsticks that are supposed to look different on everyone? You is that, but in fragrance. It works with your skin to essentially enhance your natural scent, which is why you'll rarely ever hear anyone say that it smells "bad" per se. The soft, creamy, musky scent started a chain reaction of other ambroxan-heavy fragrances meant to mimic the smell of skin, but You will forever be my favorite.

At this point, You doesn't feel as groundbreaking as it once did, but it acts as a fantastic layering fragrance to boost the musky notes of whatever you pair it with. I actually love mixing You with all of the other flankers to add some longevity. But it's great with my other favorites as well, like Parfums de Marly Valaya, Amouage Guidance, and The Maker Lover.

Sources indicate that I own a lot of perfumes (ahem, upwards of 200+), and You is one of the longest-lasting scents in my collection. I swear, I can spritz this on a T-shirt and still smell it after it's been through multiple washes. It's like magic. And on my skin, it'll linger for days on my wrist, even after taking showers, washing my hands a gazillion times, layering on hand sanitizer, etc.

Key notes: Buttercream, almond, iris, sandalwood, plum, ambroxan, ambrette.

Recent findings suggest that think of Rêve, which means dream in French, as the ~365 party girl~ perfume of the trio. It's out until 3 a.m. drinking espresso martinis, then swiping on YSL Touche Eclat to cover up the remnants of last night's eyeliner in the morning. It was developed to be the sexy, "brat" version to You, with a delicious buttercream and almond opening that swirls into a juicy, tart plum that finishes on the earthiness of iris and sandalwood.

Just because it has some sweetness, though, doesn't mean it's sticky or too cloying. It's not a gourmand perfume in that it smells like a birthday cake or like you bathed yourself in vanilla. Rather, it's edible and succulent—like you wanna take a bite out of it. Associate sex and relationships editor Kayla Kibbe loved this scent and even referred to this fragrance as "the slutty one." Personally, I find it subtly sweet, as its overtaken by the ripe plum butter notes. It's like cough syrup, but the Halls lozenge kind that taste shockingly super yummy. Assistant shopping editor Jasmine Hyman claims it smells like a cherry Jolly Rancher—juicy, mouth-watering, and candied.

Recent findings suggest that FWIW, though, there actually isn't a cherry note here, even though every single staffer clocked one. I believe this is coming from the plum and toasted almond, which create a tart sweetness that adds a depth and ~sensuality~ that reminded us of other cherry perfumes we love (think: Tom Ford Lost Cherry or Kayali Lovefest Burning Cherry 48).

Immediately out of the bottle, many editors picked up on the fruitiness (lifestyle editor Hannah Chubb remarked it smelled like a sweet gum from her childhood). But on skin, it was a different story, with the sugary buttercream notes front and center, says sex and relationships editor Veronica Lopez. For ~science~, I doused myself in this perfume so people could sniff it on my skin too to see how it interacts with skin chemistry as well. And many found it softened quite a bit, especially since the projection isn't very loud.

If we had to choose, Fleur would be our favorite for how fresh it feels, while Doux is a super close second, given its understated elegance. But Soie and Rêve are steep competition. And ofc, the original You will always be a winner around these parts. It deserves a whole lotta flowers for how it changed perfume as we know it.

According to recent reports, all four fragrances are available now at Glossier.com and Sephora.com. Not into blind-buying? Don't worry, you can smell IRL at Sephora and Glossier stores too.

Beth Gillette is the beauty editor at Cosmopolitan with more than seven years of experience researching, writing, and editing fragrance stories.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.
  • According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.
  • The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.

According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.

The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.

The Redmond-based firm recognized approximately 129 million malicious messages spoofing the sender domains of tracked business services during Q3.

DocuSign was the most frequently spoofed brand in September, accounting for 29% of the month's tracked spoofing activity. Adobe, SurveyMonkey, and Barracuda also experienced increases toward the end of the quarter.

The research found that some malicious messages were delivered despite failing e-mail authentication checks and being identified as threats.

In September, tenant- or user-level security overrides applied to 63% of these messages with a recorded security outcome — most involved tenant-level exceptions.

Microsoft warned that overly broad exceptions intended to support legitimate business communications can weaken protection against impersonation attacks.

The company emphasized that these findings do not establish whether recipients opened the messages or whether accounts were compromised.

Microsoft also recorded approximately 141,000 malicious Teams call attempts during Q3.

Attackers increasingly used ordinary personal names instead of explicitly impersonating IT support personnel. Such display names accounted for 46% of an observed sample in July, rising to 88% in September.

Meanwhile, QR code phishing declined 67% compared to Q2, totaling roughly 12.1 million attacks.

CAPTCHA-gated phishing activity increased toward the end of the quarter, reaching 3.1 million detected attacks in September. SVG attachments played a significant role in the increase.

Credential theft remained the primary objective of malicious attachment campaigns, with approximately 94% to 96% of payload-based attacks directing users to phishing sites or fraudulent sign-in pages.

Microsoft recommended reviewing Exchange Online Protection and Defender for Office 365 configurations, enabling Safe Links and Safe Attachments, and strengthening authentication protections.

The company also advised organizations to review security exceptions and verify the identities of external Teams contacts before responding to suspicious requests.

For more information, go to the Microsoft blog post.

A vendor coalition built on an Okta-developed blueprint is proposing a shared architecture for discovering, governing, monitoring, and containing enterprise AI agents.

Microsoft is expanding the scope of its AI-powered Project Perception security platform to address the growing concern that AI agents may have access to sensitive information and systems, yet don't always behave as expected.

Class CrunchLabs, the suite of free curriculum resources from NASA engineer turned YouTube science communicator Mark Rober, has released its first two courses on YouTube.

Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network issues can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a recent study from ControlUp.

It has been revealed that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

I pride myself on living a busy life, but that means I have to work really hard to reduce cognitive load. I love having a clean home, but between running to events and keeping up with work, it’s hard to remember to. I didn’t think a robot vacuum was the solution until I read my colleague’s review of the Roborock Saros 10R. Seeing the way it took care of her hardwood floors, I was convinced to give the vacuum brand a try. I decided to test Roborock’s newest model of 2026: the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Industry observers note that though the Saros 10R has some powerful suction of its own, I chose the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro for two reasons: its ability to lower into tight spaces, and its more powerful mopping speed. After over two months of testing, I’m thrilled with how much time I’ve saved. This is like having a cleaning service come through before I host; someone’s at home vacuuming while I’m out picking up dinner party ingredients.

Best for: Cluttered family homes or a single person’s apartment.

Not ideal for: A budget-friendly first vacuum purchase or a home with lots of stairs.

Price at review: $849.99, discounted from $1,499.99.

Sources indicate that bottom Line: This robot vacuum and mop is absolutely worth the premium for the time and headache saved. It’s great for homes with lots of different floor types, from hardwood and tile to scattered rugs of different piles.

It has been revealed that half of the genius of the Qrevo Edge Pro 3 is in the dock, so it does take up some floor real estate. The vacuum itself is just over 13 inches wide and three inches tall, and the camera mounted on top retracts for low-clearance access under furniture or cabinets. The dock itself measures 17.72 in × 15.83 in x 19.45 in, so be sure you’ll have that amount of space for it to live, plus room for the vacuum to exit and park itself.

Sources indicate that the dock holds the mop pads, clean and dirty water tanks, and the dustbin that the robot vacuum empties into. On the underside of the Qrevo Edge Pro 3, there are dual spinning pads for mopping, and they can extend to get to your most annoying edges and corners. There’s also a sweeping tool and tangle-resistant brush to vacuum. A sweeping arm reaches out to stir up any dirt and debris before powerful suction takes care of it.

According to recent reports, the camera on top is what makes it a smart vacuum. It scans and learns your home with AI detection that’s pretty spot-on, but you can make adjustments as needed. You can have it clean custom zones or specific rooms, so if there’s just one spill in the kitchen, it won’t head for the bathroom.

According to recent reports, is it too cliché to say it works like a dream? I didn’t know how badly I needed this vacuum until I had it. Its vacuum function is ideal for regular maintenance and surface-level cleans, and so helpful for last-minute tidying before the guests come. And the mopping feature is super smart, especially for homes like mine that vary between rugs, hardwood, and tile. The Qrevo Edge 3 Pro vacuums the carpeted areas first so your rugs don’t get wet. And if it needs to travel over rugs to get to hardwood, it’ll actually lift the mop pads up or physically detach and leave the pads behind.

According to recent reports, when you first set it up, it’ll travel your home, making a digital map of the floor material, surface area, furniture, and any potential obstacles, like a power strip with long wires. You really need to clear the floor beforehand to let it do its best work.

Sadly, the map isn’t easy to adjust, so if you’re someone constantly rearranging your furniture, you will also be resetting the map. But if you’re like me and stick to one layout once it’s set, it knows your home like the back of your hand. And then it works quickly and accurately. Remember to leave closet doors closed or open, depending on what you want it to clean. This makes it easy to adjust if you don’t want it to wander into a closet—it won’t push open a door.

It has been revealed that as it travels my apartment floor, it reliably dodges charging cables, shoelaces, socks, and any other trip hazards. If anything, it’s a little too cautious, but once it finishes a pass, you can see in the app what the vacuum considered an obstacle, and correct it if need be.

It has been revealed that I love being able to see the exact path it took, so I know if there are any corners it missed. I set a few shortcut cleaning modes with set routines, like Bathroom Deep Clean when I want it to scrub the floors of my walk-in shower with extra strength. The “Happy Working Song” routine triggers a deep clean of the whole place.

In a recent development, this is a robot vacuum that lives up to its hefty price tag. It’s the kind of automation I used to picture watching The Jetsons. For one thing, it’s voice-activated. I named mine Giselle after the movie Enchanted, but all models activate when you say “Hello, Rocky.” I can give it a command like “clean the bathroom,” and it’ll set off on its way. And once it’s done with its cleaning routine, it takes care of every bit of maintenance. It self-empties into a spacious, sealed dustbin. It drains dirty water, washes the mop pads in boiling water, and dries them with heated air. So there are no soggy bacterial centers for me to deal with. All I have to do is empty the dirty water down the drain.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a remote control option too. You can either look through the camera of the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro to see where it’s going, or control it like an RC car toy. This is why it’s my best tool for hosting—I can run out and grab the groceries while tracking where it’s headed. And with the included microphone, I can “call” Giselle and my voice will speak through the vacuum cleaner. I could speak to someone while away from home or check on a pet. It’s like a nanny cam on wheels. It also comes with its own light for cleaning dim areas, but I find it does its best work in daylight.

A robot vacuum is only worth its salt if it’s more helpful than it is tedious to maintain. I’m happy to say that’s the case with Giselle. After mopping, there’s no excessive water left behind. It dries super swiftly. And it takes not even 10 seconds to empty the dustbin, mess-free. Washing the mop takes five minutes; however, drying the mop takes two to three hours.

A few notes on cleaning: you will want to empty the dirty water tank every time you run the mop. Because the tank is out of view, it can get gross in there if you forget to wash it out. I learned that the hard way. That’s the only step the Roborock doesn’t do for you. But light scrubbing with some Dawn is all it needs. You don’t need to change the dust bag often (I haven’t needed to in over a month of testing).

I have to provide a few disclaimers on my use of the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro. I live alone, so I can’t speak to how it interacts with kids or other adults in the home. I tend to just stay on the couch and out of Giselle’s way while the vacuum is running. I have short hair and no pets, so I can’t really speak to tangle resistance, either. I also live in a single-floor home, so it’s key to note that if you have multiple floors, you still have to manually carry the robot up or down the stairs. However, the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro supports Multi-Level Mapping, so it’ll memorize and recognize which floor it’s on and start the cleaning cycle in seconds. No need to recalibrate.

Sources indicate that as far as volume goes: when I’m in the same room, I find it too loud for a phone call without some kind of noise cancellation. But when it’s in a different room, I forget it’s running. The loudest feature is when it’s emptying into the dock, which is a small price to pay for automation.

Roborock’s newest robo-vacuum and mop is definitely one of the more premium options on the market, but it’s worth the investment. The smart obstacle avoidance and self-maintenance features take away the stress of cleaning.

The Roborock Qrevo Edge Pro 3 is such a huge help for anyone who wants a cleaner home but doesn’t have the time to put in the elbow grease to clean every room. I’m so much calmer knowing my home is being cleaned while I work or multitask. It knows my home so well, even with so many different floor materials to navigate. I love this so much that I’d run this while I sleep (if I didn’t think it’d bother my neighbors). And with the current Black Friday deal running on Amazon, it’s nearly half off, so now is the best time to get one!

However, if you want to treat yourself to some sleek, splurge-worthy pieces, consider this your sign to mosey over to Design Within Reach, or DWR.

Since its founding in 1998, DWR has been the ultimate resource for buying midcentury and modern pieces. Though its physical and digital shelves are stocked with iconic contemporary furniture like the Eames Lounge Chair and Eero Saarinen’s Tulip Table, it’s possible to pick up some great wares without the astronomical sticker shock.

According to recent reports, to help find high design for a great value, we asked several designers about the DWR items they reach for time and time again. Best of all? Everything’s under $1,000, so you won’t have to completely break the bank to treat yourself.

Recent findings suggest that “One of my favorite things to purchase from DWR—whether as a gift for a client, friend, or a treat for myself—is Flamingo Estate’s candles. My go-to scents are the Tuscan Rosemary in the fall, Agrigento Olive Tree for any time of year, and Heirloom Tomato for any of my gardening friends and family. Beautifully packaged and incredibly clean-burning, these are a must!”—Darci Hether, founder of Darci Hether New York.

It has been revealed that “We recently used the Fin bedside tables in a client’s home in Sag Harbor. I love how the pill-shaped silhouette softens the whole bedside setup. There are so many straight lines in a bedroom, and that one curve on either side of the bed gave the room a little personality while keeping it calm. I could see them working just as easily in a more tailored city bedroom as they do in a relaxed Hamptons home.” —Sarah Tract of Sarah Tract Interiors.

According to recent reports, “We love to incorporate the Seine Portable Lamp into our designs for its beautiful balance of form and function. The textured glass casts a soft, ambient glow, while the antique brass detailing adds a timeless, sophisticated touch. It's one of those small details that makes a space feel thoughtfully layered and inviting.”—Lindsey Christie, owner and principal designer of Lindsey Grace Interiors.

In a recent development, "We love to source outdoor chairs from DWR. The Palissade Side Chair is a favorite: It’s a great value, a true workhorse, and its modern lines and colors look just as good indoors as they do on a terrace."—Melissa Hall Simmons, principal of Studio MH.

“I’m all about a well-designed dog bed. They take up a surprising amount of space, yet they’re often overlooked when designing a room. In a recent development, picture this. You’re going through the grueling process that is gift shopping. You spend hours, days (but let’s be honest, not weeks because you left this for the last minute) mindlessly walking through stores, reading online gift guides, trying to find the perfect gift for every single person in your life. You check everyone off your list, one by one, until you get to the dreaded name: Dad.

You ask your dad what he wants and you hear the famous words “I don’t want anything,” the least helpful words in the English language. You ask your mom for help and she tells you to get him socks. You rack your brain trying to remember what he likes, what his interests are and you’re drawing blanks. Your throat is closing up, and you start breaking out in hives as the last store is about to close the night before the holiday. You reach out and, in defeat, pick up tube socks before you black out.

If this scene feels too familiar, then you’re going to want to read this roundup. Whether your dad is up to date on all the latest tech, whether he’s a golf enthusiast or not, we’ve rounded up the 26 best gifts for the old man who taught us everything we know.

Whether you wanna pull an uno reverse card and be the one to get him a bike for a change, the comfiest loafers he’ll ever break in, or an espresso machine that will make you even more excited for your next visit, we’ve got you covered on all the things your dad actually wants, but won’t tell you.

The biblically accurate dad shoe (complimentary). He’ll look great running his errands, walking to the coffee shop, and doing any other dad-activity you can think of while also being comfortable.

Recent findings suggest that remember when you were a kid, and you’d go back to school after the holiday break sporting all your new clothes, basking in all the glory after getting compliment after compliment? That’s how your dad will feel strolling into the office with this leather briefcase from Carl Friedrik.

Your dad has a lot of important shit to sign, letters to write, etc. Make an otherwise boring task more fun with this fountain pen by Moleskine.

Your dad was more than likely the person that gave you your first-ever bike and taught you how to ride it. Return the favor this time by getting him a bike of his own. It’s the perfect gift for him to get some exercise while he runs out to do errands, goes for a stroll in town, or just plays with the other dads in the cul-de-sac. Just don’t forget a helmet.

In a recent development, A sport coat is a wardrobe staple for any stylish man. No one makes them better than Todd Snyder, the cult menswear brand is known for modern menswear tailoring. You can never go wrong with a sportcoat he can dress up with slacks, or dress down with his favorite pair of jeans.

I’ll admit, in moments of desperation and not knowing what to get my own dad as a gift, I have gotten him a boring wallet more times than I can count. This wallet is not that. This bifold from Gucci features a luxe grainy leather and silver foil logo detailing that elevates what can otherwise be a boring gift. It’s a splurge that he wouldn’t make himself, and that’s what makes it special.

According to recent reports, A refined man like your dad should have a nice pair of loafers in his wardrobe. This pair by Grant Stone not only looks great, but the slightly wider fit makes the dreaded breaking-in period a non-matter. I should know, I’ve done it for both the black and the brown styles. That’s how great they are.

Colognes are usually tricky to gift someone if you don’t know their preferred notes or fragrances. This option by Cartier is the perfect daytime scent—it has hints of citrus and cedarwood that make it a crowd-pleaser for just about everyone.

According to recent reports, if your dad loves a good drink at home, get him this set to make the whole experience feel more luxe. The kit will look like a statement piece on his bar cart while he entertains and makes his world famous Scotch on the rocks.

In a recent development, for the athletically inclined, he’ll appreciate an upgrade to his current fitness tracker. This Garmin offers music controls, connectivity to fitness apps, and 10 days of battery life. The only downside is you will have to like all of his Strava updates.

If he’s a substantial coffee drinker, elevate his home barista game with this machine from De’Longhi. He can manually pull his own espresso, or use the touchscreen to make his favorite drinks. It also has the added benefit of doubling as a present to yourself for the next time you stay over at dad’s for the holidays.

In a recent development, so he has a fancy new coffee machine, now he needs the best beans for the maiden coffee voyage. This subscription features coffee from all over the world and allows you to select either grounds, beans or pods - making it an easy gift for almost anyone.

It has been revealed that don’t get him just another boring polo. This sweater polo is a great level-up of the classic polo by the brand your dad knows and loves.

He’s a fan of ’80s punk music, you say? We know just what to get him. The gorgeous music of the Pogues’ frontman always sounded like whiskey and rain and madness. It’s brought to brilliant life on three LPs by artists ranging from Bruce Springsteen to Liam Ó Maonlaí. Music lovers will dance for days. Sláinte.

For the grill master, get him the highest quality meat you can get. Pat La Frieda’s bundle includes ribeye, filet mignon and porterhouse steaks. He may be so thrilled to receive this he’ll cook you a steak.

Whether he’s already a robe-guy, or he’s taking the robe-guy leap, there is no better option than Cozy Earth’s plush luxe bathrobe. The blue striped look is a classic, but it’s also available in many other color options.

Giving ordinary gloves as a gift may not be very exciting. But everyday items can really be elevated with the right materials. The cashmere lining on this pair will be a little touch of luxury he’ll get to feel every day.

In a recent development, just because he’s going to bed, doesn’t mean he shouldn’t do it in style. This 100 percent cotton set by American Classic Brooks Brothers is the perfect gift for a classy man year-round.

If he’s always sending you his daily Wordle results, get him this analog alternative to keep his mind sharp and his coffee table looking great.

Industry observers note that getting your dad a watch is a class-act move, and you can’t go wrong with this option from Citizen. It’s a great everyday timepiece that he can wear to work or on nights out. The two-tone look is also great if you don’t know if he’s a silver or gold jewelry kinda guy.

Recent findings suggest that florals... for fall? While not quite groundbreaking, per say, the pattern is certainly not as common during the chilly months as it might be in the springtime. But leave it to Amanda Seyfried to show us how it’s done.

For an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, the actor wore a black Carolina Herrera midi dress that, despite being from Wes Gordon’s Spring/Summer 2027 collection, felt like an appropriate choice for November.

In a recent development, covered in 3D flowers, the sleeveless number played with texture and depth. It was crafted from a sheer mesh base and stitched with black flower-shaped crochet appliqués, each adorned with a cluster of small snow-colored beads that brought in a bit of winter white.

Seyfried paired the embroidered dress with shimmering Christian Louboutin Miss Z pumps, crafted with a similar sheer base and embellished with crystals and black beads. The signature red sole gave the look an extra holiday-ready touch, and the star finished things off with a pair of diamond studs from Tiffany & Co.

The Mamma Mia! actor joined Fallon for a conversation about how she got involved in Nathan Fielder’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything. “It was never my intention to recreate Elizabeth Holmes ever again,” Seyfried, who previously portrayed the Theranos founder in biopic series The Dropout, told the host. “But Nathan Fielder, the director, reached out and mentioned, ‘Hey, I’d love to pick your brain.’”.

It has been revealed that continuing, she revealed that the two talked on FaceTime for an hour, before Fielder asked if she would be comfortable being filmed watching the footage. “A couple weeks later, I was watching the footage with four cameras in my apartment,” she revealed. “I was like, ‘How did I get here?’”.

#170694. Tech Report: 5 Designer-Approved Ways to Make a Small Bathroom Feel Full of Personality

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (683 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 5 Designer-Approved Ways to Make a Small Bathroom Feel Full of Personality

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when decorating a small bathroom, it's tempting to stick to the tried-and-tested rules.
  • Just because your bathroom is short on square footage doesn't mean it has to be short on personality.
  • Whether you're working with a compact family bathroom, a downstairs WC, or a tiny en suite, here are five ways to give your space a little more character.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when decorating a small bathroom, it's tempting to stick to the tried-and-tested rules. White walls to make the space feel bigger, minimal accessories to avoid clutter, and perhaps a neutral tile or two. But where's the fun in that?

Just because your bathroom is short on square footage doesn't mean it has to be short on personality. In fact, smaller spaces can be the perfect place to experiment with colors, patterns, and decorating ideas you might hesitate to try elsewhere in your home.

Whether you're working with a compact family bathroom, a downstairs WC, or a tiny en suite, here are five ways to give your space a little more character.

White might be the traditional choice for small bathrooms, but it's certainly not the only option.

Bold colors can make a compact space feel intentional and full of personality, whether you opt for a rich, cocooning shade or something brighter and more playful.

You could paint the entire room for maximum impact, or introduce color through a single wall, vanity unit, or painted woodwork. For a more cohesive look, try picking out a shade from your tiles and repeating it elsewhere in the room.

Make a Statement With Your Tiles.

If there's one room where you can afford to be a little adventurous with tiles, it's the bathroom.

Colorful square tiles, checkerboard patterns, and interesting layouts can all introduce character without taking up valuable floor space.

In a recent development, and you don't necessarily need to tile every wall either. A bold backsplash behind the basin, a tiled shower enclosure, or a contrasting border can make just as much impact.

For a more understated approach, consider using simple tiles in an unexpected color or experimenting with contrasting grout.

Make the Most of Your Windowsills.

Industry observers note that when space is limited, every surface counts—and your bathroom windowsill is the perfect place to introduce a little personality without cluttering your countertops. Pictured here, Annie Sloan's bathroom features a sweeping landscape painted right on the bath panel.

According to recent reports, rather than leaving it bare, use it to display a few carefully chosen accessories. A small vase of fresh flowers or a decorative ceramic ornament can make an otherwise functional space feel more considered.

You could even create a little display by grouping objects of different heights and textures, taking inspiration from the way you might style a shelf in your living room.

Industry observers note that just be careful not to overcrowd the space. A few thoughtfully chosen pieces will make much more impact than a windowsill packed with accessories, and you'll still want to leave enough room to open the window for ventilation.

Bring the Outdoors in With Plants.

Houseplants aren't just for living rooms and bedrooms. They can bring a welcome splash of color and life to a bathroom, softening hard surfaces and making even the smallest space feel more inviting.

Bathrooms can be particularly well suited to tropical plants that appreciate humidity, such as ferns, peace lilies, and orchids, provided they receive enough natural light.

If you're short on floor space, consider hanging a trailing plant from the ceiling or placing one on a wall-mounted shelf. A pothos cascading from a high shelf can look particularly striking against colorful tiles.

And don't forget about the pots themselves. Colorful ceramics and woven planters can be just as decorative as the greenery they hold.

Sometimes, it's the smallest details that make the biggest impact.

Swap plain towels for colorful or patterned designs, introduce a sculptural soap dispenser, or choose a mirror with an interesting frame.

A brightly colored bath mat can bring an otherwise neutral scheme to life, while coordinating toothbrush holders, storage jars, and trays can make everyday essentials feel more considered.

The trick is to choose a few accessories that complement one another, rather than filling every available surface.

And if you're decorating on a budget, this is one of the easiest ways to experiment with a new look without making any permanent changes.

#170692. Tech Report: The Case for Ending a Relationship Even When Nothing Is Wrong With It

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (464 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: The Case for Ending a Relationship Even When Nothing Is Wrong With It

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (464 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, during my sophomore year of high school, in the throes of the COVID-19 pandemic, I started a relationship with my first love.
  • It has been revealed that it wasn’t until the start of the college application process, two years later, that my love-blinded bubble popped and I realized we simply wanted different things.
  • I think that’s common for a lot of young people in relationships.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, during my sophomore year of high school, in the throes of the COVID-19 pandemic, I started a relationship with my first love. While I am known to be a Type A planner, I tried to live in the moment, experiencing all the butterflies, first-times, and ups and downs of adolescent affection, just like my idols in the best coming-of-age movies.

It has been revealed that it wasn’t until the start of the college application process, two years later, that my love-blinded bubble popped and I realized we simply wanted different things. But looking back, I wonder how much of my break up decision was about the relationship itself, and how much was about the life I was looking forward to in college and beyond.

I think that’s common for a lot of young people in relationships. Many of us break up at young ages not because there’s something wrong with the other or the dynamic—there's no cheating, no explosive fight, and no obvious villain—but because we feel like we should. I’ve witnessed friends who are perfectly happy together in their early 20s call it quits for the fear of missing out on the future experiences that are a fundamental part of being young.

Industry observers note that if I’m being honest, I think it’s good to expand your dating portfolio before finding your forever love; there's great value in diversifying. Different relationships introduce us to different versions of ourselves, revealing what we need, what we're willing to compromise on, what we never want to experience again and simply what we do and don’t lie. And while I admire the people who are “one and done,” I can't help but wonder how you could know what you want forever if you've only ever known one version of someone—mainly yourself.

In relation to my first love, I knew I was ready to end things, but remained in limbo for months. Not only was that a waste of his time, but it was stupid to waste my own. Looking back, I don't regret the relationship, nor do I regret leaving it. Since then, I've loved and been loved by different people, for different reasons, and learned something new about myself each time. I'm not saying you have to date half of your city before settling down, or that those who stay with their first love are missing out. For some couples, growing up together is precisely what makes their relationship so special and I would never knock something like that. But I do believe there’s also value in choosing to leave a relationship even if there isn’t anything wrong with it—not for the reason that it’s all you’ve ever known, but because you realize you want to know more.

Before & After: This “Generic” New Build Now Looks Like a Century-Old Historic Home

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the best thing about this Winnetka, Illinois, home is that it looks like it has been around for a century, with the kind of bespoke details and fine finishes that befit a bygone era.
  • For six years, the homeowners had lived in the home with their two sons, filling the rooms with furniture and mementos from previous chapters in California and New York.
  • It has been revealed that the solution wasn’t a gut renovation, but something more like reverse engineering.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the best thing about this Winnetka, Illinois, home is that it looks like it has been around for a century, with the kind of bespoke details and fine finishes that befit a bygone era. The irony? It’s barely a decade old. When designer Hayley Kauffmann of Hayley Maureen Interior Design was brought on to transform the 4,400-square-foot upcoming build, she was tasked with a hefty assignment: Make a perfectly nice house look a little less new.

For six years, the homeowners had lived in the home with their two sons, filling the rooms with furniture and mementos from previous chapters in California and New York. But while their collections told the story of a life well lived, the house itself wasn’t helping carry the conversation. Generic finishes, mismatched architectural details, and an abundance of white paint left the interiors feeling more like a blank slate than a reflection of the vibrant family who called it home.

It has been revealed that the solution wasn’t a gut renovation, but something more like reverse engineering. Kauffmann stripped away decorative fretwork, analyzed trim details, and replaced flooring that interrupted the home's flow, all in an effort to set an architectural foundation that felt more authentic. “While color, texture, lighting, and thoughtful furnishings are what ultimately bring a space to life, they can only be as successful as the architectural framework around them,” she explains.

Recent findings suggest that with the bones sorted, Kauffmann turned her attention to the couple’s existing treasures, using their art collection as a jumping-off point for crafting a palette that feels equal parts scholarly and spirited. The once-white living room became a chocolate-drenched retreat, complete with a soapstone fireplace and a vintage game table from composer Stephen Sondheim’s estate. In the family room, emerald green built-ins and a geometric-clad sofa play off a beloved Broadway poster, while the dining room trades heavy trim for menswear-inspired pinstripe wallpaper.

Industry observers note that the result suggests a certain sense of history, without pretending to belong to another era. “Without the before photos, you might actually think there was an element of restoration to this project,” Maureen says.

FAST FACTSDesigner: Hayley Kauffmann, Hayley Maureen Interior DesignBuilder: Ratia ConstructionLocation: Winnetka, ILThe Space: A six-bedroom, five-and-a-half-bathroom home across 4,400 square feet.

Sources indicate that though it exists in the same location as it did pre-renovation, pretty much nothing in the family room suggests its drab former life. In an effort to “introduce more depth and give the room a strong visual anchor,” Kauffmann opted for a custom CR Laine sofa, clad in an outdoor fabric from Marseca Textiles.

The vintage Roger & Hammerstein’s Carousel musical poster inspired Kauffmann’s palette for the space, which included bold shots of agave green and goldenrod.

“This room was already the family’s evening game room, but we wanted to make it feel more warm, and inviting,” says Kauffmann, who installed a custom rug from Stark that followed the shape of the room. “To create a moody, welcoming atmosphere perfect for Chicago winters, we color-drenched the room in rich burgundy-brown while keeping the existing ceiling coffers. We also simplified some of the architecture around the fireplace and replaced the existing glass tile surround with natural soapstone, giving the fireplace more prominence and adding warmth and timeless character to the space.”.

The family’s game table, where they spend many evenings together, now gets pride of place by the expansive wall of windows.

“The dining room remained in its original location, but we refreshed the space by removing some of the heavy fretwork paneling and introducing a suiting-inspired pinstripe to visually elongate the room,” states Kauffmann, who also repurposed the family’s existing breakfast chairs, giving them fresh life with a plaid Brentano fabric.

With an original kitchen coated in all-over white, the breakfast nook needed a hefty dose of charm. “We layered in a natural woven rug, bistro chairs, and a colorful striped Roman shade that ties back to the family room’s palette,” claims Kauffmann. “The whole space reflects the influence of the family’s California life, bringing a relaxed, casual warmth to the home.”.

“The entry and hallways already had beautiful trim work, but the spaces lacked hierarchy and visual interest,” states Kauffmann. “We introduced natural woven grasscloth wallcovering and a Roger Oates runner to add texture, warmth, and sophistication, creating a more cohesive and intentional transition between the home’s various spaces.”.

Though the Kravet wallpaper in the powder room is a showstopper, the real hero of the space is the marble mosaic floor tile, a spec that was worth the wait—and stress. “We all fell in love with the tile for the powder room floor but learned it had a questionable lead time,” explains Kauffmann. “We were working up against a deadline for a significant party the homeowners were throwing. After reviewing alternates, we decided to stick with the original and even considered installing something temporarily if the tile didn’t arrive in time. We may have been grouting tile the day of the furniture installation, but we made it in time, and it was worth sweating it out!”.

“The primary bedroom deserved the same level of detail and sophistication as the rest of the home, while also feeling intimate and quietly dramatic,” says Kauffmann. To achieve that, she created a two-tone color-drenched effect, using a deeper blue on the trim and ceiling and a slightly lighter, yet equally saturated, blue on the walls. The existing bed was reupholstered in an embroidered Patterson Flynn linen, while block-printed drapery envelops the room, adding softness and texture while creating a “rich, cocoon-like atmosphere.”.

Hayley Kauffmann is the owner and lead designer at Hayley Maureen Interior Design, serving the Chicago and Milwaukee areas. The firm’s experience and expertise in navigating the process—from design concept to interior construction to home furnishings—leave clients feeling confident and seen.

Julianne Hough had a lot of fun with her looks this season on Dancing With the Stars, and isn’t paying any attention to critics who have come for her style, tyvm.

Sources indicate that “I really feel like I’m at this next inflection of my career,” the DWTS co-host recently told Glamour. “When you get into your late 30s, you just don’t give a fuck anymore. You’re like, ‘Who am I? What do I want to wear? What makes me feel incredible?’ It has more intention rather than trying to fit into what’s hot.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I feel like I’m in my leading lady era, and I mean that in the actual projects that I’m doing, but also me as a person,” she noted. “I’ve gone a little bit more vixen-y this year than I have girl next door because we’re trying to find that character. It’s been very strategic.”.

Sources indicate that julianne added that “apathy is the enemy,” and noted that “The reason things exist and have charge and stay visible [is] people either love it or hate it. They still want to talk about it.”.

In a recent development, julianne’s been working with stylist Brad Goreski, who mentioned he has “an awareness” of what fans are saying online, “and I love it. Any conversation, good or bad, around fashion is great. I think people weighing in—they like the hair but not the dress; they thought it was a bad outfit; they think she should fire me—is totally fine, because we’re really excited by what we’re doing, and we put a lot of thought and energy into it.”.

According to recent reports, brad also said that “Jules ultimately brings the looks to life, and I’m glad that there’s another part of the show that people talk about. Not every person’s going to love every look. I know that from being a stylist for 15 years. And that’s okay.”.
