Rocco’s Essential Fridge Is an Entertaining Game-Changer—and at Its Lowest Price EVER Right Now

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1146 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor.
  • Industry observers note that we rarely think of our fridge as the sexiest part of our home.
  • It has been revealed that I’m a proud beverage girlie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Industry observers note that we rarely think of our fridge as the sexiest part of our home. Even less so a mini fridge, since it often reminds us of college party days. Rocco has been the brand to change that, with their viral Classic Fridge that’s in every cool-girl apartment (including Senior Commerce Editor Marina Liao’s). But the longstanding grievance people have with it? The price. So when I heard they launched a new fridge—The Essential—that’s even colder but $800 cheaper? I had to try it for myself.

It has been revealed that I’m a proud beverage girlie. I keep a triple coaster at my desk for when I switch between Diet Coke, iced coffee, and water throughout the day. A considerable amount of my fridge space was dedicated to canned drinks. The Rocco Essential fridge let me return my produce drawer to its original function. And then it became so much more. Scroll on to find out how it elevated my hosting game.

Best for: Hosting in small spaces (it doubles as a bar cart!).

Not ideal for: Storing perishable drinks like juices, shakes, or dairy.

Price at review: $995, discounted from $1,195.

Bottom Line: The Rocco Essential is the sleek younger sister to its viral Classic, and the Sight System takes the guesswork out of grocery shopping. You’ll always know how much wine you have at home.

Industry observers note that at its baseline, the Rocco Essential Fridge is a souped-up mini fridge, specifically designed to be the best home for your beverages. It can hold a grand total of 27 bottles of wine or 77 12-ounce cans, but an optional expansion pack increases that to 105 cans. It comes with six racks, each with indentations that keep your cans and bottles from rattling around. Every drink is stored on its side, and each shelf slides in and out easily without getting stuck. They can be removed and repositioned to accommodate bigger bottles, like two-liter sodas and Champagne.

The Rocco Essential right now comes in three colors: cream, sage, and graphite, each with a brown-tinted glass facade. The matte silhouette of the fridge is pretty sleek on its own, but there are optional add-ons to make it blend into your home a bit more. You can add a two-in-one oak serving tray and cutting board to the top, or swap the metal handle for a matching wooden one.

The most powerful feature is its compressor, made with the same technology as Sub-Zero fridges. It supports three cool-down modes: Smart, Quiet, and Party. Party mode offers rapid cool-down that’s great for high-traffic use (or cooling lukewarm sodas bought last-minute). Quiet mode uses a slower cool-down with less noise, and Smart switches between Party and Quiet as needed. And the compressor noise peaks at 39 decibels—library quiet.

It has been revealed that the Essential Fridge has many of the same benefits as the Classic—same powerful compressor, same app controls, and same beverage tracking database. One of the biggest changes is the look. The Essential has a more neutral color range than the pops of color in the Classic, and swaps a reeded glass facade for a warm tint.

The Essential’s main compromise is its single temperature zone, compared to the dual temperature zones of the Classic. In the Essential, if you have specialty wine that needs to be stored at a certain temperature. The rest of your drinks will have to be at that temperature too. That noted, the Essential is Rocco’s coldest fridge, getting down to 34ºF instead of the Classic’s 37ºF.

Both glasses are UV-rated, but the Essential has a dual-layer to the Classic’s triple. The Classic has slightly improved insulation because of this, but the tinted glass facade of the Essential keeps the state of your fridge’s interior more private. It also has a safety feature that the Classic doesn’t. The Essential comes with a childproof lock, which is extra important as the fridge is closer to the ground and easier for kids to access.

The Rocco Essential is my new best friend when I’m hosting. It’s so beautiful that I placed it just past my entryway, and without fail, guests coo over it when they see it. This also makes it easy for me to offer a cold beverage the second someone walks in the door, helping them settle in.

Recent findings suggest that the technology is stunningly easy to use—you can either control it with the iOS app or the slim control panel on the top of the fridge. But honestly? It’s a set-it-and-forget-it gadget, quietly humming along in the background. Sodas, wine, ready-to-drink cocktails, and cold brew are all kept ready to go. I’m impressed by how many cans or bottles can fit on one shelf, especially if you use mini cans. The bottom rack has a narrow clearance overhead, so I use that as my skincare drawer. I’m sure this confuses the app, but an ice-cold eye mask in the morning is too good to pass up.

What the Rocco Fridge is truly known for is its Sight System. The Rocco app controls the light and temperature, but it’s also connected to an ever-expanding beverage database. Its camera actually recognizes the drinks you place on each rack. Sometimes the drinks need to be rotated in order for the system to recognize them, but the app will let you know if this is the case. The fridge does a fresh scan every time you open or close the door. So, if you remove a soda, it will revision the quantity. You can check the app while you are away from home, say, picking up refreshments for a party, and you’ll know exactly what you’re working with. If the app doesn’t recognize your drink when you first add it, give it a few days, and it’s usually added to the database.

Industry observers note that the Rocco Essential is smaller than a typical full-size fridge, but it does take up considerable square footage. It functions as a high-tech bar cabinet would, so it’s the kind of piece you want to design around.

Industry observers note that the Rocco Essential fridge is the best gift you could ever give a frequent host. It’s eye-catching but minimalist. There’s no condensation on the fridge’s exterior, so you can store your favorite glasses or cocktail garnishes right on top. Even though I know I’ll be downsizing my home soon, I’m determined to keep it (or switch to their Mini Mini fridge). If you’re ready for a Rocco fridge of your own, the Essential is less than $1,000 for the first time EVER this Black Friday.

To combat this and revive my parched, eczema-prone skin, I’ve been using the Carepod One Plus, which has truly been a lifesaver.

Sources indicate that every time a friend or family member asks about it, I simply say: “Get it; it’s so easy to clean and functions perfectly.” In fact, this is what I told my sister-in-law, who was asking me about it this week because right now, Carepod is running an excellent Black Friday deal on all its humidifiers with up to 38 percent off. (Its website deal is better than the Amazon discount, too!).

I have the Carepod One Plus, which I originally got for $350 last year, and it’s now discounted to $224.25! You’re saving $125.75, and the more Carepods you add to your order, the more you save. If you need more than one for your home, it’s better to stock up on a few to properly arm your rooms against the dry winter air, as each device covers up to only 500 square feet unless you opt for the cube-shaped one that covers 700 square feet. Personally, I prefer the rounded, soft shape because I think it looks prettier on my dresser, which is where I keep mine.

I ran mine every night while I slept last winter, and it helped keep the moisture level in my space balanced. My face and eyes didn’t feel dry when I woke up, and my nosebleeds completely stopped! I knew it was time to take out the Carepod again this month when my nosebleeds started coming back in the mornings. (I store it away in my closet during the summer and bring out my dehumidifier instead.).

It has been revealed that I chose the Carepod over other popular models on the market mainly because it was created by a doctor in South Korea (with the country’s advancements in the beauty and dermatological space, I knew the Carepod would be well designed). I liked that it had a stainless steel water tank versus a plastic tank and that there aren’t too many parts to clean. My previous humidifiers all had crevices that were hard to see and clean and would inevitably get moldy over time. I don’t have to worry about any of this with the Carepod because there are no “weird” parts you can’t clean. The whole device feels quite sterile.

It has been revealed that the only cons of this product are that the Carepod does take up a decent amount of surface space unless you get it on a stand, and it doesn’t come in any other color except white. However, when it comes to humidifiers, I prioritize function over looks, and the Carepod is simply the best. With the Black Friday deal running right now, I plan to scoop up another Carepod or two to give as gifts. I know I’m not the only one who suffers from dry air come winter, and I want my family to experience the magic of this device too.

Industry News: The Launch: November’s Must-Know Fashion News

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1249 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Fall is in full swing, and with it, so is the fashion industry.
  • Where: Online at moncler.com, rickowens.eu, select Moncler stores, and Rick Owens flagship stores.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Fall is in full swing, and with it, so is the fashion industry. As the leaves continue to turn and preparations for the holiday season get serious, brands are finding latest ways to celebrate with exciting new capsules, collaborations, and stocking-worthy releases. Look no further than J.J. Martin, whose new book, Table Energy, explores the art of Italian entertaining, and the Rimowa x Maison Margiela collab, which turns travel into something even more desirable. Plus, there’s plenty of reason to get out and shop, with the likes of L/Uniform, Danielle Frankel, and Bulgari all opening new storefronts. Below, all the fashion news to know this month.

What: Fall/winter 2026 collection.

Where: Online at moncler.com, rickowens.eu, select Moncler stores, and Rick Owens flagship stores.

Industry observers note that why: Moncler and Rick Owens return to their shared winter universe with a collection that makes outerwear the main event. Quilted jackets arrive in oversized shapes, punctuated by metal studs, utility pockets, and a strap that lets you carry them when the layers come off. The palette stays pared back—black, silver-toned Palladium, Cloud Grey, and Grease—with matching boots and sunglasses to finish the look. In a black-and-white campaign photographed by Owens, screen legend Joe Dallesandro, known for his turn in Andy Warhol’s Superstars, brings his own countercultural history to the collection. “Little Joe mythologized an indifferent beauty in Lou Reed’s hymn to queer subculture,” Owens stated in a statement. “‘Take a Walk on the Wild Side’ was a turning point for me and a lot of other suppressed kids of my generation. his inclusion in Avedon’s photos of Warhol's entourage illustrated the magic of finding one’s tribe, for better or worse.”.

Moncler + Rick Owens Combo Flight Down Bomber Jacket.

Moncler + Rick Owens Cotton Blend Cargo Skirt.

Moncler + Rick Owens Trailgrip Pentalace Ankle Boots.

Where: Online at gap.com and in select Gap stores.

Why: Zac Posen is keeping things simple this winter season—and the latest GapStudio wardrobe is edited to just 12 pieces. The designer’s capsule gives familiar staples a sharper feel through sleek silhouettes, precise tailoring, and touches of unexpected texture like a playful teddy bear coat rendered in a cozy caramel fabric. Other highlights include elevated essentials that Posen has prioritized at the brand: a turtleneck maxi dress, a sleek poplin shirt, and high-rise seamed stirrup jeans. “For winter 2026, we wanted to move beyond traditional occasion wear with versatile pieces designed to be worn from day to night,” Posen said of the collection, which came to life on singer EJAE in the accompanying campaign, in a statement. “There’s still that level of drama with thoughtful tailoring and exaggerated lines, but it’s balanced by a focused palette that feels elegant and wearable.”.

GapStudio Turtleneck Maxi Dress.

GapStudio Brannan Bear Teddy Jacket.

GapStudio Structured Poplin Shirt.

Where: 31 East 72nd Street, Newly introduced York.

Why: Parisian leather goods label L/Uniform is making its New York debut with a flagship on the Upper East Side. Following boutiques in Paris and Tokyo, the store marks the brand’s first American address with founder Jeanne Signoles working with architect Jakob Sprenger to create a space that balances the polish of a boutique with the practical spirit at the heart of the label. “Opening a store in New York was a priority for me from the very beginning,” Signoles indicates. “I always felt that L/Uniform naturally belonged here, with the city’s energy, its independence, and its very strong connection to everyday life. Our bags are made to be used—to work, to travel, to accompany daily life.”.

L/Uniform Nº146 The Cross Body Bag.

L/Uniform Nº131 The Mini Press Bag.

Where: 6 Harrison Street, Fresh York.

Recent findings suggest that why: A historic Tribeca landmark is the setting for Danielle Frankel’s new flagship. At 6 Harrison Street, the bridal house has created a 12,000-square-foot space where original architectural character meets a considered, contemporary interior by Augusta Hoffman Studio. Private rooms make space for a more personal appointment, while the wider setting invites visitors to explore the collection at ease.

Danielle Frankel Chantilly Lace Degradé Border Drop Veil.

What: High jewelry collection and new boutique.

Where: 237 Worth Avenue, Palm Beach, Florida.

Why: A 1920s Palm Beach estate is a fitting setting for Bulgari’s first U.S. presentation of “Eclettica.” Designed by Addison Mizner, the waterfront home hosted a gala that also marked the opening of the house’s latest boutique. Venus Williams, Chanel Iman, and Becca Bloom were among the guests, with Jewel performing. The collection includes 15 transformable designs—the most Bulgari has presented in a single collection—alongside more than 50 high jewelry pieces. With its Roman roots and sculptural approach to high jewelry, Bulgari’s “Eclettica” brings a distinctly Italian point of view to Palm Beach.

Who: Rimowa and Maison Margiela.

What: Limited-edition collection.

Where: Online at rimowa.com and maisonmargiela.com and select Rimowa and Maison Margiela stores.

Why: Some things look better after they’ve been lived in. That idea is at the heart of Rimowa and Maison Margiela’s new travel collaboration, which brings together two signatures: the German luggage house’s familiar grooves and Margiela’s hand-painted white Bianchetto finish. Designed to change with use, the suitcase and matching bag will take on marks and patina as they travel. A campaign by Dexter Lander brings that idea to life in a Haussmannian apartment, where the white paint seems to spill beyond the pieces themselves.

Rimowa x Maison Margiela 5AC XL Bag.

Rimowa x Maison Margiela Classic Cabin.

What: Bird on a Rock installation, window displays, and holiday décor.

Where: The Landmark; 727 5th Avenue, New York.

Why: Tiffany & Co. has switched on the holiday season at The Landmark, with Amanda Seyfried leading the way. The actress lit the flagship’s Bird on a Rock installation by placing an ornament on its Blue Box tree, marking the third year of the display and a full-circle moment. Seyfried stars in the house’s fresh holiday film, “You & Me,” which travels between present-day New York and a memory from the ’90s. Mikey Madison, Jordyn Woods, and Louisa Jacobson joined the celebration.

Tiffany & Co. Bird on a Rock Wings Narrow Ring.

It has been revealed that tiffany & Co. Bird on a Rock Pendant.

It has been revealed that tiffany & Co. Bird on a Rock Earrings.

Industry observers note that why: Just in time for the holidays, La DoubleJ founder J.J. Martin has released Table Energy, a newly introduced book about the art of Italian entertaining, with a foreword by fashion writer Leandra Medine Cohen. Its pages move from alfresco lunches to candlelit dinners, all in the colorful, convivial spirit of La DoubleJ. The book made its debut at the brand’s Upper East Side boutique, The Lighthouse, where Martin, ELLE Decor’s head of editorial content Elisa Lipsky-Karasz, and ELLE editor-in-chief Nina Garcia gathered to celebrate l’art de la table.

What: Limited-edition collection.

Where: Online at tecovas.com, aninebing.com, and select retail locations.

Why: Anine Bing has a new way to kick up a look. The designer has teamed up with Tecovas on a capsule that reworks the label’s Loretta and Jamie boots with star embroidery and polished goat leather. Cowboy hats and belts round out the lineup, which introduces alongside Anine Bing’s spring/summer 2027 collection.

Tecovas Anine Bing x Tecovas Loretta.

Tecovas Anine Bing x Tecovas Jamie.

Tecovas Anine Bing x Tecovas Plaque Buckle Belt.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it’s no secret that Apple has been dominating tech headlines this year. But between the news of its recent price hikes on MacBooks and iPads and the release of the iPhone Duo (the tech giant’s first foldable), not much fanfare has been made about the new generations of the Apple Watch. As far as we’re concerned, that’s a damn shame, because they’re well worth the upgrade—especially if you can find one on discount.

Right on cue, Amazon’s Black Friday sale is here, and with it comes record-low prices on every Apple Watch, whether you want to shave $100 off the brand-newly introduced Apple Watch Series 12, take advantage of a sub-$200 price on the entry-level Apple Watch SE 3, or score the rugged Apple Watch Ultra 4 while it’s just $650.

SHOP AMAZON’S BLACK FRIDAY SALE.

Below, we’re breaking down the differences between each model—and peeling back the curtain on our price-tracking prowess—so you’re all set to shop. After all, when Apple gadgets are this cheap, they tend to go like hotcakes, so don’t say we didn’t warn you when they inevitably sell out.

Commerce editor Luke Guillory argued that compared to other fitness trackers on the market, Apple was lagging behind with its lack of readiness score functionality—until now. The Apple Watch Series 12 marks the debut of the brand’s very own readiness score thanks to a revamped tracking system. Plus, the watch now measures your heart rate more frequently to deliver Heart Rate Variability (HRV) readings every five minutes. If you’re trying to pay closer attention to your health this year, it’s a smart buy, made sweeter when it’s on sale for Black Friday.

Given that this brand-newly introduced watch dropped to just $350 for October Prime Day, we were expecting more of the same for Black Friday, so this $100 discount, bringing it to just $299, is all the more impressive.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for Apple’s most affordable watch, we suggest turning your attention to the entry-level Apple Watch SE 3. It was actually the watch that converted Gelbart to Apple wearables in the first place, arguing that its beauty is in its simplicity.

“It's an accurate and predictive workout tracker. It counts my steps and activity and connects to my phone to play music and receive messages and calls,” he says. “If you’re latest to the Apple Watch and want to dip your toes, this is where I recommend you start.” It has the same sleep tracking features, like nightly sleep score and sleep apnea notifications, but lacks the ECG app or hypertension notifications of its newer siblings. It also has an 18-hour battery life so you’ll need to charge most nights.

This $179 Black Friday deal drops the SE 3 even lower than its previous record-low price of $199, which we first saw during October Prime Day, making the most affordable Apple Watch an even smarter buy.

Our editors have loved every version of the Apple Watch Ultra thus far, and the latest model not only delivers on greatness once again, but also just hit a record-low price for Black Friday. Earlier this week, this was a then-best $100 off, but now that Black Friday proper is here, Amazon did us a favor and shaved another $50 off.

Sources indicate that the Apple Watch Ultra 4 has the same fresh Readiness features and advanced health tracking the Series 12 has, in addition to the dive functionality, ruggedness specs, and satellite capabilities we’ve come to know and love from the Ultra line. Plus, from a sartorial standpoint, it’s hard to beat the new semi-translucent watch bands, which took design cues from the ocean.

Recent findings suggest that our philosophy when it comes to shopping for Apple tech during Black Friday? If you find the watch with the features you need at a price you can stomach, pick it up. It’s incredibly likely that the deals you see here are the best ones you’ll see for the rest of the year.

Industry observers note that you’ve reached the point in your holiday gift-shopping journey when you have to figure out what to get the woman in your life who already has everything. If your mind feels like absolute mush and you genuinely have no idea where to start, don’t worry—that’s completely normal (trust us, we’ve been there). This list of unique gifts for the gal who seems to own it all already is here to save the day.

As someone who would consider herself that girl (come on, I review products and shop for a living!), I can tell you that thinking outside the box will always win me over. And it doesn’t have to be anything extravagant, either! Maybe it’s a monogrammed pouch, a cozy blanket, a cool journal, a beautiful claw clip, or something she’d never think to buy for herself. It’s all about finding the surprises that feel thoughtful, personal, and just unexpected. Ahead: 50 gift ideas she won’t see coming.

Look at you thinking ahead, you! Great question. To keep things short and sweet: It’s almost too late, but you can still beat the clock with a few methods. USPS recommends shipping by December 17 for its Ground Advantage and First-Class Mail services, December 18 for Priority Mail, and December 19 for Priority Mail Express. UPS and FedEx can get a package there in time for Christmas as long as you ship by December 23 at the very, very latest (and shell out some extra cash for overnight shipping). This week: Lame duck kicks off with Hegseth impeachment effort

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Massie of Kentucky told CQ Roll Call in late October that the Hegseth impeachment resolution would come up in the first week of the post-election lame duck session.
  • The lame-duck session of Congress kicks off this week as the House is expected to consider a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth while the Senate seeks to advance a bipartisan deal on permitting reform.
  • Last week’s midterm elections saw Democrats claim sizable majorities in both the House and Senate in the new Congress, and among the immediate questions is whether the demoralized GOP will face attendance woes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Departing GOP Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky told CQ Roll Call in late October that the Hegseth impeachment resolution would come up in the first week of the post-election lame duck session. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

The lame-duck session of Congress kicks off this week as the House is expected to consider a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth while the Senate seeks to advance a bipartisan deal on permitting reform.

Last week’s midterm elections saw Democrats claim sizable majorities in both the House and Senate in the new Congress, and among the immediate questions is whether the demoralized GOP will face attendance woes.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the expected next speaker of the House, said Sunday that he would support the Hegseth impeachment.

“I'm a hard 'yes' on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries said on ABC’s “This Week.” “The so-called secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go.”.

Departing Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., told CQ Roll Call in late October that the Hegseth impeachment resolution would come up in the first week of the post-election lame duck session.

Sources indicate that it’s also orientation week on Capitol Hill for latest members of Congress. House orientation got underway Sunday.

The Senate, meanwhile, looks to take up a bipartisan permitting bill that has the backing of President Donald Trump.

“This Landmark Permitting Reform Legislation will codify our America First Energy Agenda, and ensure that we can build Pipelines, Mines, and Power Plants faster than ever before, lowering Energy Costs for American Families, and creating High Paying American Jobs,” Trump posted on Truth Social.

Senate negotiators over the weekend released text of an amendment seeking to address remaining concerns.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m grateful for the input throughout this process from Senate and House colleagues, environmental and labor organizations, and Tribal leaders. Our manager’s amendment improves [the bill] and addresses the thoughtful feedback we have received,” Senate Environment and Public Works ranking Democrat Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island said in a statement. “Now it’s time to pass this bill so we can lower costs, juice the clean energy economy, build substantial things again in America, reduce pollution, and create tons of new well-paying union jobs.”.

Beyond the permitting bill, the Senate Republican majority may seek to use its remaining time trying to confirm more of Trump’s nominations before the control of the floor agenda passes to the Democrats.

Recent findings suggest that "We've got the farm bill, the NDAA, and we have that third reconciliation bill that we need to get across the finish line, and there are so many things that we need to get done and buttoned up," including nominations, departing Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., said in a weekend Fox News interview. Blackburn, one of the Republicans who had success at the ballot box, is now governor-elect of Tennessee. But it's an open question how long lawmakers will want to stick around.

In a recent development, there’s also the matter of an imminent fight over funding the government and laying the groundwork for the fresh Congress. Republican leadership elections are scheduled for Tuesday, while Democratic leadership elections are expected in December. Democratic senators-elect are due on Capitol Hill Monday and Tuesday, according to the office of Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y. Schumer is widely expected to be the majority leader in 2027.

There have been some calls for Senate Republicans to delay their elections, though current Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota has been widely expected to remain as the Republican leader.

Industry observers note that “One of the things I learned in business and the Army is that after a failure, you have to start with honesty, transparency, and accountability,” Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., said in a Sunday night statement. “As I’ve shared with Leader Thune, I don’t believe we should move to leadership elections until we have digested and debated the lessons of the midterms and how to move forward.”.

It has been revealed that sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., has also been circulating a letter calling for a delay, and he has argued the election should not be held, in part, because the makeup of the Senate Republican Conference is not yet final. Senate races are still not called in Alaska and Mississippi.

Absent this week will be Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who recently had a stroke.

Industry observers note that “The doctors are very encouraged by the progress I’ve made so far. In order to take my recovery seriously and get back to work on the quickest timeline possible, I will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center after being discharged from the hospital today,” Murphy said in a Friday statement.

Recent findings suggest that if you want your gifts to arrive by Christmas, you’ll need to strategy ahead—especially with holiday shipping volume peaking in December. For USPS, the recommended ship-by dates this year are Dec. 17 for Ground Advantage and First-Class Mail, Dec. 18 for Priority Mail, and Dec. 20 for Priority Mail Express. FedEx and UPS have similar mid-December deadlines that get more expensive the closer you get to Christmas Day. Some mega-retailers like Amazon offer two-day delivery or overnight shipping depending on what you're ordering and the delivery location. The short answer? Order soon and always check the estimated delivery date before you buy.

‘Political malpractice’: Calls grow to delay Senate GOP leadership elections

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1081 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ron Johnson, R-Wis., walks through the Ohio Clock Corridor this summer.
  • After last week’s midterm elections saw them lose at least seven Senate seats and the majority, some Republicans are pushing for a reckoning, saying the conference should stop and think about its future.
  • “After the stunning defeat [we] just can’t continue on business as usual.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., walks through the Ohio Clock Corridor this summer. Now he’s pushing to delay leadership elections for his conference, urging a discussion of last week’s larger than expected losses. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

After last week’s midterm elections saw them lose at least seven Senate seats and the majority, some Republicans are pushing for a reckoning, saying the conference should stop and think about its future.

“After the stunning defeat [we] just can’t continue on business as usual. That kind of defeat demands change,” Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., remarked on Monday evening.

It has been revealed that asked if he himself would want to run for Senate minority leader, the Wisconsin Republican responded with a question of his own: “That’s part of our problem. Who’d want the job? Would you want it?”.

Though no hopeful had emerged as of Monday afternoon — at least publicly — to challenge current Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., for the top GOP post, the frustration was palpable as Republican senators returned to D.C. and grappled with the election results. Calls grew throughout the day to delay the conference’s leadership elections planned for Tuesday morning.

“Well, I mean, I’m open to hearing what the arguments are for that,” Thune told reporters Monday when asked about the possibility of postponing the leadership votes. “I don’t know if that solves anything, but like I mentioned, it’s going to be a decision that’s ultimately made by Republican senators. We’ll hear them out.”.

Industry observers note that johnson told reporters on Monday that if the election is held, he would “leave the room” and walk out. Either way, he seemed certain to at least get a “fulsome” discussion of the topic, as he requested in a letter he sent to Republican Conference Chair Tom Cotton, R-Ark. Four other Republican senators signed on to the letter, hitting the threshold to call a conference meeting under internal GOP rules.

Also signed by Sens. Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, Rick Scott of Florida, and John Kennedy of Louisiana, the letter obtained by CQ Roll Call cites last week’s “stunning defeat” and reads in part: “Holding leadership elections without engaging in a robust discussion and evaluation of how those running for leadership intend to lead would be political malpractice.”.

Kennedy said Monday evening that he was asking to postpone the leadership elections because “we need time to talk to each other.”.

“We’re like a shop owner who’s losing his customers. It’s not the customer’s job to fix that. It’s the shop owner’s job, and I’m not looking for blame-shifting. I’m looking for self-examination,” he mentioned, adding that he wouldn’t consider running for minority leader himself.

In the letter, the group asked that at the time the leadership elections were set to begin, 9 a.m. on Tuesday, they instead “have a fulsome conference discussion and delay holding leadership elections until we all have a chance to hear from leadership candidates as to what type of collaborative conference governing model we should adopt and what our strategy will be to counter the emboldened Democrats.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that that is now a thing of the past.
  • Black Friday is still filled with great deals—you just have to know where to look and what to expect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How do you even define a good deal anymore? The whole point of Black Friday was for retailers to make us wake up at the crack of dawn the day after Thanksgiving, wait in line, and then fight someone over a TV that was 50 percent off at Sears or Best Buy. How did they do that? They would sell a few products (doorbusters) at a loss just to physically bring people into the store. Those deals were good, and everything else, which you would buy because you were already there, was where the money was made.

Sources indicate that that is now a thing of the past. Lines and physical altercations aside, in the past 20 years there has been a real swing in the favor of major retailers. First, we created Cyber Monday (though most people do their Black Friday shopping online already). Then the deals started a week earlier. Now, they last all month. And instead of having door busters to get you in the door, retailers just have very aggressive online marketing programs. In fact, it turns out that most Black Friday deals aren’t even deals at all. In a recent study, it was found that one in three Amazon Black Friday deals provided no true savings at all—prices were marked up earlier in the year, only to be brought back down to a standard retail value. The big retailers like Amazon and Walmart are the most to blame for these tricky strategies, but you should still be judicious when looking at any so-called Black Friday sales.

The good news? Black Friday is still filled with great deals—you just have to know where to look and what to expect. A lot of massive wins revolve around private sales at more niche, direct-to-consumer stores. For example, Filson, one of our favorite outerwear brands, is having a 25-percent-off sale for Black Friday. That’s not the 75-percent-off you might have wanted, and there are other times that Filson goes 25-percent off. But the best strategy these days is to think about holiday shopping: Just buy the things you already would, but do it while they’re on sale now.

You should be especially skeptical of tech products. The increase in all tech prices has made it easy for those brands to push a 10-percent-off sale when products were 10-percent-off the current price. This is the sort of stuff we’ve been watching as the sales roll around. Based on this and years of covering sales and knowing what’s good and what’s not, we determined these are the best deals of the weekend. These are the deals our editors think are actually worth shopping this Black Friday.

Mr. Porter has an absolute goldmine of a sale. Like sure, you can grab this Brunello Cucinelli Jacket for $6,500 at 50 percent off. But it’s also filled with basics from brands like On that rarely go on sale.

Industry observers note that fortela is our favorite luxury westernwear brand with Italian design sensibilities. If you pay full price, you get every dollars’ worth in quality and concept. But shopping its archive sale and saving 50 percent? That’s highway robbery.

In a recent development, A cashmere-blend overcoat for 30 percent off is a real steal. Use code BLACKFRIDAY before it sells out.

According to recent reports, A few days ago, the Samsung Frame Pro was 50 percent off. That deal was real, and it sold out. Today the Hisense Art TV (which we’re fans of) is 50-percent off. These deals vary daily, but today, this is the one we’d buy.

Dyson deals are confusing as fuck. You need to be knowledgeable about the model you’re buying into, and here that number matters. You will be able to find models like the V8 and the V10 for super cheap this week—but that’s because those models are old and outdated. Right now, the best and newest Dyson cordless vacuum is the V16—with all the bells and whistles, it retails at $1,100, but it’s $200 off right now.

Industry observers note that but as someone who has used every Dyson, I know the V12 is a damn good model. And while it isn’t the newest, it still has lots of the same features as newer models and will last you years. So the fact that it’s on sale for $400 this weekend makes it a truly good deal. Also, I can’t find this deal on Amazon. For the best deals from Dyson, I would always check its actual site.

As previously mentioned, we love that many of Filson’s jackets are 25 percent off this week. This is a good example of when a brand just wants to participate in a sale, so they’re willing to mark down popular items. This jacket is so good our commerce editor Luke Guillory endorsed it last week, calling it the best $250 jacket. Guess what? Now it’s only $187. We know for a fact that this deal won’t last past Black Friday.

Industry observers note that it’s expensive, yes, but Begg x Co. is one of the best cashmere brands anywhere in the world. $500 off a new cashmere sweater is something that doesn’t happen until the end of the season. But if you buy it now, you still have six good months of wear to get in.

Industry observers note that water filtration has become very expensive, especially when it comes to reverse osmosis and a countertop version that looks sleek. We have been recommending this one for over a year at $500, so the fact that it’s $150 off for once makes it a pretty good deal.

Furniture on sale is a whole category we can’t ignore. Furniture markups are a real thing, and a lot of it has to do with quality and materials. Marble is overpriced for sure, but good quality marble is worth it. We love Soho Home’s marble, and this dining table has been one of its most popular pieces for a while. Getting it for almost $3,000 off when you’re not a member is a major deal.

If you’re on the home redo kick, then a brand like Le Maé, which is offering some of its best wood pieces at 50-percent off, is a great place to start. Made with high quality materials and oak, this is one of those furniture pieces you will own forever.

If you’re a camo guy or do any non-deal hunting, then you know that Tom Beckbe jackets never go on sale—but this is your lucky week.

Newly introduced Congress will still be filled with losers

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Capitol Dome is illuminated before dawn on Oct.
  • OPINION — Once again, the next Congress is going to be filled with losers.
  • According to recent reports, this is not a personal judgment about their character or personality, but a simple recognition that many members have lost races before getting elected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Capitol Dome is illuminated before dawn on Oct. 13. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

OPINION — Once again, the next Congress is going to be filled with losers.

According to recent reports, this is not a personal judgment about their character or personality, but a simple recognition that many members have lost races before getting elected. And the incoming class is no different.

Industry observers note that I’ve written many versions of this column for more than a decade, and yet the lesson always seems to get lost, no pun intended. Parties routinely attack candidates who enter a race with losses on their record. And, of course, it happened this cycle as well.

“We beat him once. We’ll beat him again,” National Republican Senatorial Committee Chairman Tim Scott declared when Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown declared his challenge to appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted in the summer of 2025.

“Ohioans gladly sent him packing last year, and they’ll not hesitate to toss him aside again,” mentioned a Republican strategist.

Brown lost reelection to Republican Bernie Moreno in 2024 but came back to defeat Husted for the state’s other Senate seat. And Brown is far from the only candidate to avenge a loss with an electoral victory last week.

It has been revealed that the fact of the matter is that losing a race doesn’t have to be the end of a political career. Losses can lay the foundation for future success by building name ID or a fundraising network. Or sometimes it takes a change in the political environment or change in circumstances, such as running for an open seat instead of challenging an incumbent.

In addition to Brown, there are more than a dozen losers coming into the next Congress:.

In some instances, though, the losses are piling up.

Republican Rep. John James of Michigan now has three statewide losses on his record. He lost Senate contests in 2018 (taking 46 percent of the vote) and 2020 (48 percent) and came up short in his bid for governor this year (44 percent).

According to recent reports, republican former Sen. John E. Sununu of Upcoming Hampshire, who lost reelection in 2008 to Democrat Jeanne Shaheen, fell in his comeback attempt for the open seat last week.

But they could take heart from another repeat loser. Charlie Crist, a former Florida governor and congressman, has had a handful of high-profile losses over the years, including for Senate and two gubernatorial comeback bids. He was just elected mayor of St. Petersburg.

So even though I know it’s a futile request, let’s have a bipartisan agreement not to attack candidates for past losses, because losing doesn’t mean they can’t later pull off a win.

If you’re looking hard enough for sales on menswear, you can almost always find a discount on something decent, a pair of shoes, a shirt maybe, but you have to scrounge. Every other week of the year, that’s just how it is. But this week, the week of Black Friday, the opposite is true. Every store and their mother is having a sale and suddenly, it’s not easy to tell which markdowns are gonna go fast and which ones will still be there when you log on again in December. Luckily, you have me. Year-round, it’s my job to keep tabs on deals so I know which ones to pounce on this Black Friday.

Sources indicate that on Amazon, there’s my favorite Lacoste polo, which is actually on an outrageous sale going up to 40 percent off if you’re the right size. Filson jackets are 25 percent off. Lululemon isn’t just for the gals, it has a ton of great stuff for men and its Black Friday sale is absolutely stacked. And REI is doing its classic “We hate Black Friday but are doing a sale anyway” thing, and as always we are here for it.

Let’s start with the personal favorites; after that we’ll just list deals alphabetically by brand. First, Amazon. Yeah, yeah, everything is Amazon now. But when Bezos is offering significant discounts on Lacoste polos and Levi’s, we listen.

Nothing is ever going to beat the cool of a beat-to-hell Filson jacket. If you’ve been holding off on buying one, I can’t recommend it enough. Plus, Black Friday is the perfect time to get one for 25 percent off.

FIlson Tin Cloth Insulated Jacket.

I tell regular—meaning normal guys, not fashion-y dorks like me—that Huckberry is really the answer to 90 percent of what they want. All of a man’s casual wardrobe can be bought here; the only thing it doesn’t stock well is suits and tailoring. I’m seeing up to 40 percent off on seasonal shirts, and up to 30 percent off jackets, sweaters, and pants; that’s as good as it gets, folks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

With the new third season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians on Disney+, this is a great time to dive into Rick Riordan’s books, whether you’re reading them for the first time, rereading them, or picking up where you left off once upon a time. In true camp fashion, here’s your itinerary for reading all of the Percy Jackson books in order. (Or the Camp Half-Blood Chronicles, if you’d prefer to call them that.).

According to recent reports, in the world that Riordan has created, demigods roam the Earth in modern times. For the most part, they’re indistinguishable from regular kids. Some of them, like Percy Jackson himself, don’t even know that their parents are literally figures from Greek and Roman mythology. Since there are so many of those centuries-old tales, Riordan has been able to turn them into a ton of young adult adventures.

In the first book, Percy Jackson learns that he’s a demigod and enrolls at Camp Half-Blood. He meets Annabeth Chase and Grover Underwood, and the three of them go on a quest to find Zeus’ lightning bolt.

This time, the teenage demigods go looking for the Golden Fleece. They’re joined by Tyson, Percy’s brother who happens to be a cyclops.

It has been revealed that in the third book, which happens to be the basis for the current season of the Disney+ series, the group expands and they go on a rescue mission. For who exactly? You’re going to have to read to find out!

Camp Half-Blood is under attack (again), and our heroes enter the mythical Labyrinth to save it from invading forces.

In the (original) grand finale, the fight moves from Camp Half-Blood to Manhattan.

Fifteen years later, Riordan returned to his original hero with a duology about Percy’s last year in school. This means quests and college applications.

The final (unless there’s more) book is set at Halloween as he pet sits for Hecate. Should be easy!

But wait, there’s more! Riordan has dozens of other stories, long and short, in this universe. Here’s enough to get you started:.

This is a series about a group of seven demigods who embark on a quest together.

This series is, like it says on the tin, about Apollo.

Nico also appears in Heroes of Olympus. This continues his story.

This series is set in the same universe, but all about Egyptian mythology.

These short stories are Percy Jackson and Kane sibling crossovers.

This trilogy is about Annabeth’s cousin and his dealings in Norse mythology.

It has been revealed that the most recent book, co-written by Annabelle Oh, has a female protagonist: Katie Kim, daughter of Ares. It will get a sequel called The Rite of Aphrodite in March 2027.

Sources indicate that we’ve come a long way since our skinny jeans era, but even though they never entirely left, they somehow got an iffy reputation. The good news is you can still wear them this season, perhaps just tucked into a pair of knee-high boots. Jeans and knee-high boots are the classic pairing that never disappoints this time of year.

However, skinny jeans aren’t the only style that works. Nowadays, relaxed and even slightly baggy denim is also taking the spotlight in this combination. If you’re wondering how to make the look feel current, it all comes down to proportions. Pair slim jeans with a chunkier knit or an oversized coat to balance the silhouette, and let looser denim do its thing tucked under the boot shaft for a more modern approach.

Not convinced? Below, we’ve rounded up some inspiration for how to wear your favorite boots and jeans together this season.

According to recent reports, this timeless look never disappoints. Pair black skinny jeans with a matching turtleneck, a ’90s-inspired plaid blazer, and burgundy boots for an outfit that gives off effortless French-girl style.

#170612. Why Is Fashion So Obsessed With Distressing?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Elle ↗ Open Full Page

Why Is Fashion So Obsessed With Distressing?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in 2026, the runways are ripe with notes of distressing and deconstruction.
  • In a recent development, with 2008 fashion on the rise, too, maybe we’re closer than we ever thought to going back to ripped jeans.
  • Sources indicate that but why is fashion obsessed with looking worn out right now?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in 2026, the runways are ripe with notes of distressing and deconstruction. For fall/winter 2026, Prada sent crystal-covered embellished heels down the runway with perfectly pointed toes that looked as if they had just accidentally graced a puddle of distinctly dirty Latest York City rainwater. The same is true for the label’s menswear collections: deliberate stains, frayed fabrics, and wrinkles were intentional and core to the aesthetic. At Miu Miu and Coach, leathers were aged. And for spring/summer 2027, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Valentino, Diesel, and JW Anderson showcased elements of worn-in style, with damaged, repaired, dirty, and distressed looks dominating. After seasons of quiet luxury defined by minimal, poised, and perfected aesthetics, something about fashion’s new love affair with mess feels refreshing.

In a recent development, with 2008 fashion on the rise, too, maybe we’re closer than we ever thought to going back to ripped jeans. Ann Demeulemeester, Balenciaga, and Diesel seem to think so, as all of these labels put frayed jeans on the runway for the spring/summer 2027 season. Ann Demeulemeester creative director Stefano Gallici brainstormed his latest collection on a journey through the Californian desert, and in the show notes mentioned intentional wear, via “Ceremony tailoring worn to death, or to eternity.”.

Sources indicate that but why is fashion obsessed with looking worn out right now? Valerie Steele, director and chief curator of The Museum at the Fashion Institute of Technology, thinks there’s never been a better time for it. “There is kind of a crisis in fashion right now,” she tells ELLE. “Fashion has started to seem really out of touch with real life and real people.” One example: luxury fashion’s pricing is so high right now that some brands, like Gucci, have revealed that they’ll be reducing prices by as much as 30 percent. Also: “There is kind of more of an interest in what ‘real people’ wear. You know, what does it mean to be authentic? I mean, in many ways, I would say that authenticity is a chimera. You know, it’s a mythical beast that doesn’t really exist in a totally commodified, late capitalist world,” indicates Steele.

According to recent reports, steele notes the damaged jeans of the Y2K era, ’90s grunge moments, and earlier punk movements as similar examples. Deliberate distressing has also been famously done and documented by some of the greats, like Vivienne Westwood, Rei Kawakubo, and even Alber Elbaz, also coinciding with unique moments in time when economics and politics made it all the more interesting and, in some cases, ironic. “Fashion is supposed to be upcoming and transgressive,” says Steele. “So, if scuffing your shoes is gonna make them more fashionable, then you go for it, right?”.

According to recent reports, intentionally distressed, messy fashion has been around for hundreds of years, however. “We also saw it actually with some male dandies in the second half of the 19th century,” indicates Steele. “You also had some of that sensibility in New England in the late 19th century when wealthy people in Boston would go to Paris and buy their couture clothes, and then they just keep them in a trunk for a year, so they wouldn’t be so new when they were worn for the first time. It has a lot to do with the idea that the sort of shiny newness of fashion may seem a little bit fashion victim-y. They weren’t having to show off that it was brand new.”.

In case there was any doubt that the distressed effect is just another example of insular runway fashion, people are actually buying ripped, stained, destroyed clothes outside of the designer space, too. Just look at Distressed Fest, a biannual, bicoastal vintage clothing pop-up event focused on heavily worn, threadbare, and destroyed garments that are sold for a premium. Scuffs, rips, stains, and all: as ironic as it may be, fashion’s current status symbol now is looking like you’ve been through something.

It has been revealed that every guy needs the best beard trimmer for his situation. Whether he grows it patchy, keeps it perma-stubbled, or is as lustrous as the A-List beards, a trimmer is mandatory in every beard kit. And not all beard trimmers are alike, which is why the best one for your facial hair style may be different from the next guy’s.

I tested a bunch of beard trimmers to deliver you a real who’s who of men’s grooming devices. This list reflects a range of options—some multitaskers, some detailers; some top-shelf, some a better buy for lower budgets. Above all, though, I ask you this: Make sure that the device you choose allows your beard to reach its full potential. That doesn’t mean you need a massive bushy beard, but rather, you should be able to achieve whichever style (or a suite of styles) you want to wear over the next few years—which is the minimum amount of time any of these devices should last. Ideally, they’ll hum on for five to 10 years, anyhow.

Here are the best beard trimmers after we tested pretty much every last one of them. (And while you’re at it, consider my rosters of other grooming tools, from razors and electric shavers, to manscapers and hair clippers.).

It has been revealed that black Friday is here, and the deals are hitting fast. For the biggest and swerviest markdowns, editor favorites, and elite-level shopping intel, keep it locked on our roundup of the best Black Friday deals and best Black Friday clothing deals.

It has been revealed that no sense in burying the headline: Philips Norelco’s Multigroom 9000 Series is, hands down, the best beard trimmer you can buy. And that’s before factoring in how much more it can do than just keep your facial hair in check than other electric razors that are found in your everyday grooming kit. (It’s also recently been renamed the “All-in-One 9000” but answers to both names.) For the last 5 or 6 years, this has been my single go-to trimmer. Everything else is trying to dethrone it, and so far, no true contest has emerged. In terms of customization and power, this device checks all of the boxes.

Recent findings suggest that it all starts with the beating heart: "The Multigroom does not compromise on power or battery life, and it's very intuitive to use," states Fellow Barber’s Head of Education Emily Clark. The battery life truly over-delivers: your mileage may vary since Philips Norelco only claims a (still impressive) six hours of charge, but I got a ridiculous 17 hours of consecutive runtime fresh out of the box, thanks to a lithium ion battery. Speaking of the box, there’s a lot in there, all of it useful. Between the small tooth-like detail attachment and foil shaving head, the Multigroom 9000 makes it easy to style and sculpt with precision. One trimmer even adjusts by tenths of a millimeter to help you get the perfect designer stubble, if that's your aim. And that’s just its beard trimming bona fides. The Multigroom 9000 is also a solid hair trimmer (shout out to that brawny motor and battery again) and body hair trimmer as well. Covering off for three products, and doing it well, suddenly makes the $90 price tag look like a deal.

According to recent reports, long-term testing notes: Wouldn’t you know it… I lost the beloved little shaver on this one recently. Heartbreak. (Yeah, I can test a upcoming one, but I realize now how much of my love for it is pinned on that micro shaving attachment.) I stand by the fact that it’s the best on the market, but without that shaver, the window has opened for me to spend time with other devices, like the Braun below. Let this be a lesson: Don’t unpack your Philips Norelco all-in-one in a hotel room without carefully auditing every single piece when you pack it up again. Adam Hurly.

It offers most of the same steel-bladed precision and customization benefits as its fancier family member, albeit in a less durable body (plastic instead of stainless steel) and half the battery life. The Philips Norelco Multigroom 5000 is great for anyone on a budget, but it’s not “budget.".

Sources indicate that whereas other lower-priced beard trimmers can’t handle precise detailing, the Multigroom 5000 includes a detail trimmer and nose trimmer, not to mention hair clipper and body trimmer guards for versatility. It does lack the shaving detailer and the body shaver (as does the in-between 7000 model), which is important to note if you want that level of customization and don’t otherwise own a detail shaver that you also rely upon for bare-faced stretches of facial real estate. For this reason, I find it a little less perfect across the board compared to the 9000, but the price-to-precision ratio is hard to match. And if you want a great value above all—and a straightforward beard trimmer—meet your optimal Multigroom, the 5000.

Long-term testing notes: Recently, I used the 5000 consistently, and got quite cozy with it. Sure, it lacked the key shaving features of the 9000, but I think this is truly the best value device in the game when you only want a trimmer. Terrific muscle, terrific customization, great endurance. Five stars for this one. Adam Hurly.

It has been revealed that if you’re researching beard trimmers, you’ll see the term “zero-gap” a lot. So, what’s a zero-gap trimmer? A zero-gap trimmer cuts as close to the skin as possible, effectively a 0mm cutting length. That can make them dangerous for novices, as you can easily cut your skin or ears while you trim. But for the highest possible level of precision, that’s what you want. (The Bevel Trimmer can also be adjusted so it has a slightly longer taper.).

What is the best beard trimmer?

There’s no denying: The Philips Norelco Multigroom 9000 is the best beard trimmer you can buy these days. If its $100 price tag is too steep, the baby-brother Multigroom 5000 is a solid fallback. It’s not shower-proof, has a shorter warranty (five years to the 9000’s eight years), has a plastic body instead of steel, and comes with a few less attachments. But at $40, it gets the basics done nearly as well as it’s pricier sibling.

Can you use a beard trimmer to cut head hair?

Beard trimmers are not meant to be used as hair clippers, since clippers require much more power to cut through thicker patches of hair. However, some beard trimmers have the muscle to multitask, and they’ll proudly hype that skill—usually by declaring the work for “beard and head” or similar language. We usually verify those claims against product reviews, too. And frankly, we’d probably just opt to buy a dedicated hair trimmer (you can find our roundup of the best hair trimmers here), especially if you’ll be using it often.

Which beard trimmer do barbers use?

Barbers choose tools to suit the job, from adjustable trimmers for controlling length, to detail trimmers for sharper edges. The Wahl Pro Series High Visibility is our professional pick for precision work, while the Philips Norelco Multigroom range offers broader versatility. For home use, start with your beard length and the kind of maintenance you do most often – a tool built for crisp outlines won’t necessarily include the guards you need to trim a longer beard evenly.

Which trimmer number is best for a beard?

In a recent development, that's going to depend on what beard style you're going with. In order to play around with trimmer numbers, we like the Braun All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 9440 for its easy-to-use adjustment wheel.

How do you use a beard trimmer?

First, wash and dry your beard so you're starting off with a clean canvas. Then, decide how short or long you want to keep that bad boy. Trim against the grain of your growth, and know that the direction of growth may vary even in similar locations on the face. It's OK to make a couple of passes to ensure you get each hair because a patchy beard is a bad beard. Finally, clean up the neckline with some sharp lines so it's neat and tidy, framing the perfection that is your beautiful facial hair.

How do I maintain and clean a beard trimmer?

Sources indicate that switch it off and disconnect the charger before cleaning, then remove trapped hair from the blades and combs after each use. Follow the instructions for your particular model – a washable cutting head doesn’t mean the whole handle can go under the tap. The Remington Vacuum trimmer, for example, has removable washable parts, but its body should stay out of water.

Let washed components dry before putting them away. Oil the blades if the manufacturer tells you to, but don’t assume every trimmer needs it. Philips’ current Multigroom blades are designed to work without oiling. Replace a damaged or persistently blunt cutting unit with the correct part for your model.

How do I choose the right trimmer if I have sensitive skin or ingrown hairs?

In a recent development, avoid “zero-gap” trimmers, which is a trimmer that cuts as close to the skin as possible, effectively a 0mm cutting length—those can mess your skin if you're prone to irritation or ingrowns. Otherwise, since you're trimming, you usually won't have to worry about irritating your skin because the blades shouldn't ever actually make contact with your face.

What’s the best way to travel with a beard trimmer—any TSA or voltage concerns?

It has been revealed that one of the big concerns for frequent travelers—at least in the USA—is whether they're going to be able to get their beard trimmer through security and not having it buzz during transport. If this is a priority for you, look for a model with a travel lock like the Braun All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 9440, which prevents the trimmer from turning on in transit.

How do I clean a waterproof vs. non-waterproof trimmer?

In a recent development, waterproof trimmers are a breeze: Just hit ‘em with the (usually included) cleaning brush, then wash them off in the sink before drying and applying some oil. Non-waterproof trimmers just skip the rinse, so you’ll have to take extra care with the brush. You can also use spray cleaners specifically designed for grooming electricals depending on your trimmer's care instructions.

What should I do if my trimmer starts pulling hair or losing power?

Industry observers note that first, make sure you've thoroughly cleaned the trimmer. Next, make sure it's fully charged and/or has new batteries. If it's still pulling hair, it's probably time to swap the blades (plenty of companies sell refills on their site, and make sure to check the warranty to see if you qualify for a fresh set). If it's losing power, it might be time to swap the internal battery (check your warranty!) or get a new trimmer altogether. Luckily, we haven't had that issue with any of the trimmers listed above.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A group of incoming members of Congress and staff arrive on Capitol Hill for new member orientation on Monday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

What happens when more than 100 members-elect descend on Capitol Hill a week after Election Day?

As Rep.-elect Dan Koh, D-Mass., put it, “It really is like high school — but it’s fun high school.”.

According to recent reports, trainings and guest speakers aren’t everyone’s idea of a fun time, but Democrats are feeling good about this year’s latest member orientation. Giddy, even.

Sources indicate that the incoming freshmen will pose for a class photo on the House steps. They’ll test their luck in a lottery to see who lands the best office space. And everywhere they look, they see signs of the blue wave that swept over the country.

Recent findings suggest that “I think — well, I hope — that we will be doing a lot of exceeding expectations in this caucus. The American people deserve it and expect it,” said Rep.-elect Sam Forstag, D-Mont., as he headed to lunch after an orientation session on Monday.

Forstag is the first Democratic congressman from Montana in 30 years, succeeding retiring GOP Rep. Ryan Zinke. A former smokejumper who parachuted into remote forests to put out wildfires, Forstag won by more than 3 points in a district President Donald Trump carried by double digits in 2024.

Industry observers note that “I think there’s a lot of folks who didn’t expect us to,” he mentioned of his win. “Nobody knew who we were this past December when I was still working at the smoke jumper base in Missoula.”.

Democrats are still digesting their larger-than-expected wins, which saw them flip more than 40 House seats and oust a number of high-profile incumbents, including National Republican Congressional Committee Chairman Richard Hudson, R-N.C.

“It’s like drinking out of a firehose,” said Rep.-elect Rebecca Cooke, D-Wis., who unseated incumbent GOP Rep. Derrick Van Orden in Wisconsin’s 3rd District.

Cooke and her opponent clashed during the campaign over his use of AI-generated ads that she described as deepfakes. Now, they have to work together to make sure the transition goes smoothly.

“The congressman noted that he’s willing to be helpful in that transition. I think it’s key that we make sure that the casework is transferred over, that constituent service is a priority, and that nothing falls through the cracks for people,” she said.

The 120th Congress will be full of history-makers, and a record-breaking number of women are set to serve in the House.

Industry observers note that “This is a Congress with the most women ever to be a part of this chamber,” Cooke stated. “And a lot of [Democrats], frankly, from the Midwest, and so I’m excited to build that sort of power from the Midwest to make sure that our interests are represented.”.

The math isn’t lost on Republicans navigating a freshman class where they have fewer peers than they hoped.

In a recent development, “I thought that it would probably go a little bit different. I think a lot of people did, but it is what it is. You work with what we have,” mentioned Rep.-elect Mark Lamb, R-Ariz.

But just like high school, everyone’s trying to make friends. As incoming members filed into the Capitol Visitor Center on Monday morning, Rep.-elect Cait Conley, D-N.Y., introduced herself to Rep.-elect Sydney Gruters, R-Fla.

Meanwhile, Rep.-elect Claire Valdez, D-N.Y., who describes herself as a “proud democratic socialist,” walked by chatting with Del.-elect Robert White, who will become only the third person in the modern era to hold the title of D.C.’s nonvoting delegate.

“I’m sitting next to a teacher right now; I’m sitting next to the mayor of Scranton … good, nice people,” stated Rep.-elect Zack Mullock, D-N.J., who said he was surprised by how many “regular people” he was meeting among the incoming class.

Rep.-elect Brad Lander, D-N.Y., who ousted fellow Democrat Dan Goldman in a Brooklyn-based primary before cruising to victory in the general election, was also making friends.

Sources indicate that “I was hanging out with Donavan McKinney yesterday in orientation, and I’m just really excited to meet all the amazing people. Micah Lasher, we were hanging out last night. Jacqui Irwin, so we’re just trying to get to know each other,” he noted.

It has been revealed that after arriving on Sunday with suitcases in hand, the future freshmen got a chance to set foot inside the House chamber later that day. Lander said he’d been there before to see Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, a friend of his, get sworn in four years ago. But Sunday was his first time on the floor itself.

“It’s obviously a lot different when it’s you,” he mentioned.

Koh agreed, saying “everyone in that room, Republican or Democrat, had a lot of reverence for where they were.”.

“I think it was just a good reminder about how despite all the division, that’s what we’re going to focus on — trying to figure out how to get things done for the American people,” he said.

Members-elect were trying their best to navigate their newly introduced workplace on Monday, many of them donning backpacks as they came to terms with the realities of their new job.

“We just have to get back to class,” said Rep.-elect Ed Gallrein, R-Ky., to a crowd of reporters trying to flag him down as he left orientation to use the restroom.

They’d have Italian food for lunch, after a session in the CVC auditorium where many of the future members typed notes on their laptops.

It has been revealed that “They’ve got a packed agenda for us all week, really helping us figure out how to get started. Build our team, set course, understand where the bathrooms are — large and small. We got a lot to learn,” Lander said.

I am not the first person to point out that MacBooks are expensive. I will not be the last. If you monitor this stuff like we do, you’ll have seen the irony that Apple released the budget-conscious MacBook Neo earlier this year—only for the global computing shortage to almost immediately raise the price from $599 to $699.

But the Neo is still cheap. You could buy it for full price and get your money’s worth—although scoring it on sale makes the whole thing even sweeter. As part of its admittedly impressive Black Friday sale, Amazon shaved $50 off of the 256 GB version and $100 off of the 512 GB model with Touch ID. Chalk it up to a Christmas miracle.

Apple 2026 MacBook Neo (256 GB).

Apple 2026 MacBook Neo (512 GB).

Industry observers note that designed as Apple’s answer to the lower-budget laptops running Windows, the Neo’s target audience is technically students—hence the good branding and cool colors. That being said, if you need a personal computer for watching Netflix and doing your taxes but don’t want a full desktop, it’s a perfect choice.

According to recent reports, the Neo runs on Apple’s A18 Pro chip—the same one that powers the iPhone 16 Pro and Pro Max. If the idea of buying a laptop that runs on a phone chip gives you pause, your stress is better channeled elsewhere. While this isn’t the right device for someone who is planning to run heavy-duty software, it can handle standard Internet browsing, video calls, and the like with ease. Just keep in mind that it has only 8 GB of RAM, so it’s best suited to basic workflows. And in addition to double the storage space, the 512 GB model also features Touch ID.

Of course, this computer has the added benefit of four jazzy color options: blush and citrus for the bold, indigo for those more subdued, and silver for that classic MacBook aesthetic. Wrapped in an aluminum body with a 13-inch Liquid Retina display, the Neo weighs in at just 2.7 pounds (same as the MacBook Air) and is 0.5 inches thick. (For reference, the iPhone 17 Pro Max is 0.35 inches thick.).

Sources indicate that despite our best efforts, we don’t quite know how Apple determines its deals for major sale events. Other MacBooks—including the brand-new M6 and touchscreen MacBook Pros—are up to 23 percent off for Black Friday, but barring a Cyber Monday surprise, it looks like this discount is as good as it’s going to get for the Neo right now.

Made from ballistic nylon, which is a fancy way of saying it can take a beating. The bridle leather handles keep it handsome enough for a meeting, all while being tough enough to survive getting tossed in the back of a truck he doesn’t own.

The official footwear of the guy whose favorite trail runs from the couch to the fridge. Cozy enough to lounge in all weekend and good-looking enough that he’ll “accidentally” wear them to get the mail.

#170594. Redistricting battle could spill into 2028

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (950 w)
